Requirements: Your application is your opportunity to share your story and ambitions with the Admissions Committee. We take a holistic approach to reviewing applications, which means we consider all aspects of your professional and academic background. We encourage you to be reflective and authentic, and to approach your application as a way to help us get to know you as a person and as a professional. A complete application includes the following: a current résumé, one required essay (with an optional second essay), a GMAT or GRE score, unofficial transcripts, and one letter of recommendation. We also require a technical skills self-assessment and a video interview.

Description: Accountants love efficiency, and an MS in Accountancy from Simon Business School is the most straightforward path toward career growth in this field. If you come to Simon with an accounting undergraduate degree, the program can be tailored to broaden your skills in different areas. You may work with the Office of Student Engagement and the program faculty director to tailor your individual MS in Accountancy program. [13] The program of study for the MS in Accountancy degree is a lock-step program that meets all the requirements for a STEM-designated program. The STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) designation signals analytical rigor to employers and also offers international students the opportunity to extend their Optional Practical Training (OPT) by 24 months—for up to three full years of US work eligibility without and H-1B visa. [13] Every MS in Accountancy graduate qualifies to sit for the CPA examination in New York State and obtain subsequent licensure. [13]
ScholarshipPercentage: More than 90% of incoming MS students receive merit-based scholarship support. [19]

Requirements: The application checklist on the Simon Business School PhD admissions page includes a business-formatted résumé (not a CV) of no more than two pages, responses to two required essay prompts (with an optional third), and three recommendations. The school seeks students who are analytical, creative, committed, and eager to study complex business problems.
Fees: All Simon PhD students receive a full-tuition scholarship for all courses approved for their curriculum. [14]

Description: The Simon Business School PhD Program in Accounting provides students with the opportunity to make substantive contributions to the literature by taking advantage of the Simon School's strong economics and quantitative training. At Simon, accounting is not viewed as a separate academic discipline, but as an integral part of applied economics. By studying accounting and accounting phenomena from the perspective of an applied financial economist, an accounting researcher can provide evidence that potentially affects such diverse areas as the theory of the firm, corporate finance, the economics of regulation, and capital market efficiency.
ScholarshipAmount: Admitted PhD students qualify for an annual fellowship for five years of study and student health insurance for the duration of their program. [14]

Description: The English Graduate Program offers comprehensive training in all the major periods of British, U.S., and global Anglophone literature, as well as the history of the book, literary and cultural theory, postcolonial studies, digital humanities, performance studies, and feminist and sexuality studies. One of our particular strengths is African-American literary studies, in which we have a large group of faculty and students. Our curriculum provides rigorous training in literary history and form. At the same time, we offer courses in the general area of cultural studies, as well as those that engage in historical and current debates about class, race, gender, and sexuality. [1]

Fees.1: $2,150/Credit Hour

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Literary Translation
Requirements: To apply to the program students must have: Bachelor's degree or higher in related field; Complete the online application; Official transcripts; Three letters of recommendation; Personal statement describing: Career and educational goals; Prior experience with literary studies, creative writing, translation, and languages other than English; Proficiency in a second foreign language and literary tradition. Translation sample (approximately 20 pages of fiction or drama, 200 lines of poetry) and copies of corresponding pages from source text*. [3]
Description: The Master of Arts in Literary Translation Studies (MALTS) is for those preparing for careers as literary translators. Students who enter this program have at least a bachelor's degree in a related field such as language and literature, and they will have significant knowledge of at least one literary tradition and foreign language. [1] The program is a 30-credit program made up of three components: core, electives, and an annotated thesis translation. [3] The core introduces students to the theories and problems of literary translation. [3] For electives, students may pursue advanced study of specific national literatures or international literature as a global phenomenon, and may also choose to intern at a literary press. [3] The program culminates in a book-length literary translation into English, accompanied by commentary on the translation process, which is expected to be of near-publishable quality. [3, 4]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music Education
Requirements: Applicants for the Master of Arts (MA) in Music Education at the Eastman School of Music should apply to this program if they are interested in a more flexible degree program where they may elect courses from applied study, conducting, liberal arts, and courses at the Margaret Warner Graduate School of Education and Human Development. Admission to the MA degree does not require a performance audition but does require an interview and a musical skills assessment. General prerequisites include a bachelor's degree from an institution of good standing. A strong emphasis is placed on writing and research skills. Teaching experience is strongly recommended. [7, 8, 9, 10]
Description: The Master of Arts in Music Education is designed for students with a high standard of musical skill, breadth of musical and general educational preparation, and skills in academic writing. Teaching experience is strongly recommended. The curriculum includes courses in research methods, measurement and evaluation, curriculum, and the history and philosophy of music education. [4] Students will also take instrumental and choral methods and techniques courses and select from a variety of elective courses, including theory, composition, or orchestration. [4] The program culminates in a field project or thesis. [4] This degree has a strong emphasis on writing and research skills and can be pursued through full-time study or through a summers-only option. [3, 4, 8] The MA option has research as a secondary focus and does not require an audition for admission, though applied study at the secondary level may be included. [8]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [13]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music Leadership
Requirements: Applicants will hold an undergraduate degree or its equivalent in music. They will possess a high standard of musical skill and show breadth in musical and academic preparation. They may have professional experience in performance, education, or administration. Applicants applying to Masters of Arts programs at Eastman are required to submit an online application which collects a personal statement, a résumé, a music-related research paper, and transcripts (must represent all collegiate study). [1]
Fees.1: $60,318 for 27 total units for the Fall/Spring 2026-27. [3]
Description: The online Master of Arts in Music Leadership degree program is designed for musicians who seek to lead traditional or non-traditional musical arts organizations. [4] This degree combines engaging online learning, courses from Eastman's performance and scholarly offerings, and hands-on experience through the capstone project. [4] Drawing from a musical background, graduates will be able to assume leading roles in musical arts initiatives of all kinds, connecting with leaders in the Eastman community and beyond. [4] The backbone of this degree is a combination of intense online coursework and hands-on experience with leading musical arts organizations and mentors. [4] Full-time students complete the program over 14 months, starting in either mid-May, coinciding with the start of the University of Rochester summer schedule, or mid-January. [4] The degree can also be pursued on an extended timeline, through part-time study over multiple years, as it is designed to be flexible to students' needs. [4] Students will advance their creative mindset, sharpen their decision-making ability, and utilize case studies to continue their individual artistic growth. [4]
Accredidation: The Eastman School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [2]

Description: The Musicology Department at the Eastman School of Music provides students with creatively designed courses that explore the intricacies of musical meaning and aesthetics in widely divergent historical, cultural, and geographical settings. The department's approach is intensely interdisciplinary and informed by the rich musical environment of the school. It offers both an MA and a PhD, with the MA being available in either musicology or ethnomusicology as separate degrees. The faculty's expertise covers a broad range of subjects including opera, jazz, Renaissance sacred music, gender studies, ecomusicology, and the intersections of music and politics.
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. The Eastman School of Music, part of the university, is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Description: The MA in Pedagogy of Music Theory prepares students for a career of teaching success. With pedagogical coursework and opportunities to teach at all levels of the undergraduate curriculum, students graduate from the program with the experience and skills to teach college-level theory independently. The MA in Pedagogy of Music Theory is often pursued jointly with graduate study in performance and composition.
Accredidation: The Eastman School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [2]

Entering MA students should have a strong background in mathematics, including three semesters of calculus (through multivariable calculus), a course in linear and/or matrix algebra, and a year of probability and mathematical statistics. A course in real analysis is encouraged; a course in statistical methods is also recommended.

Of the 32 credits, at least 24 must be in departmental courses primarily at the 400 level or above. A typical program for the MA consists of PhD-level courses taken in Semesters 1 (three courses), 2 (three courses), and 3 (two courses); however, MA students have the option of completing the program in two semesters (four courses per semester). A balanced program is worked out with the student's advisor.

General application materials include transcripts, a personal statement, a resume, and three letters of recommendation. Admission to the MA degree does not require a performance audition but does require an interview for applicants who pass the pre-screening process. A repertoire list of significant works studied in the last 5 years is also required. [2]

Rather, the MA is awarded to a student in the MA/PhD program in music theory after satisfying one foreign language requirement and after completing 30 credits (with at least nine credit hours of non-theory electives) in the course of study for the PhD in theory with a grade of B or higher. [13, 16] MA students must pass a final exam if finishing with the MA only, or pass a qualifying exam in order to move on to candidacy for the PhD. [13, 16]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is an accredited institution and a member of the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [14] The University of Rochester has been accredited by MSCHE since 1921. [14]

ProgramName: Master of Business Administration in Master of Business Administration

Description: The Full-Time MBA at Simon Business School is a two-year, STEM-designated program that equips students with a strong foundation in business fundamentals and the analytical and leadership skills needed for success. The curriculum is built around a core of economics-based and quantitative-driven courses, with a focus on problem-solving and decision-making. Students benefit from a collaborative learning environment, a diverse and accomplished peer group, and a dedicated career services team. The program also offers a wide range of elective courses and experiential learning opportunities to allow for specialization in various functional areas.
Accredidation: The Simon Business School at the University of Rochester is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

Description: Engage in coursework that delves deep into leadership, innovation, entrepreneurship, international business, and public policy. Our curriculum is designed to empower you to navigate diverse, complex challenges with precision. Immersive learning opportunities, a rigorous academic environment, and distinguished faculty provide a curriculum truly tailored for the executive. The EMBA program spans five terms, with each term consisting of four course sessions (blocks). Classes meet once a month, Thursday-Saturday, offering a flexible format designed to accommodate executive students' busy professional schedules. The initial three terms in the program are dedicated to core courses that are meticulously designed for progressive learning, with each course building a strong foundation for the next. In the latter two terms, you'll encounter intellectually stimulating elective options along with the opportunity to engage in independent studies to align your academic journey to your career aspirations and interests.

With a curriculum rooted in economics and statistics, you’ll learn how to analyze all sides of a business problem and make data-driven decisions that drive success. The Professional MBA is a flexible program, allowing you to take the number of courses that works best with your schedule each quarter. Classes are offered in the evenings with some hybrid and online options available. You can complete the program in as few as 2.5 years or take up to five years, with the average completion time being 3-3.5 years.
Accredidation: Simon Business School is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).

[4] General application materials include transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, two letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, a current resume or curriculum vitae, and a writing sample. Description: The Master's in Public Health (MPH) degree program in the Department of Public Health Sciences is a 43-credit online/on-campus program accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). The MPH program has a long-standing tradition of training a diverse range of public health and health professionals in the skills needed to identify, prevent and solve community health problems. [6, 12] Upon completion of the MPH degree program in the Department of Public Health Sciences students will be able to: utilize concepts and theories of public health in addressing specific population health concerns; formulate and answer questions related to population health improvement among diverse populations, using quantitative and qualitative evidence; and; work collaboratively to identify assets and problems, collect relevant data and devise and evaluate programs. [6] Our MPH program takes advantage of our unique setting within a leading School of Medicine with its clinical research resources and collaborative faculty. [6] Active faculty research programs encompass a range of areas, including behavioral interventions, environmental health, global health, health policy and outcomes, maternal and child health, medical decision making, nutrition, and aging. [6] Our MPH program draws students from a wide mix of disciplines and backgrounds, who learn and grow in an academic environment that nurtures innovative scientific inquiry, intellectual discussion, diversity, and both personal and professional development. [6] Students completing the program will be well prepared for professional careers focused on public health practice and research in the public health and medical fields, as well as careers in private industry, government, and non-profit agencies. [6]
Accredidation: The Master's in Public Health (MPH) degree program in the Department of Public Health Sciences is a 43-credit online/on-campus program accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). [6, 12]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Specialty
Requirements: Applicants must have a Bachelor's degree in nursing from an accredited school with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0. [6] An RN licensure from New York State is required. [6] Additionally, applicants for the Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner specialty must have one year of RN experience in acute care. [6] A statistics course with a grade of C or above is also necessary. [6]
Description: The Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner program prepares you to diagnose and treat adult and older adult patients in acute care settings. As an adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner, deliver advanced nursing care to adult/older adult patients to help restore health, prevent complications, and navigate patients and their families across acute care settings. [15] Nurse practitioners in this specialty help care for adult or older adult patients who are acutely ill or have conditions requiring complex chronic specialty care. [15] Adult-Gerontology Acute Care NPs typically practice in ICUs (cardiac, medical, surgical, trauma, neuromedicine), hospital inpatient floors, and outpatient specialty care clinics. [15]
Accredidation: The baccalaureate, master's, and Doctor of Nursing Practice programs at the University of Rochester School of Nursing are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education. [2]

Description: Simon's STEM-designated MS in Business Analytics program combines a rigorous analytical curriculum with an economics-based approach. The program is designed to equip students with the theories and practical frameworks needed to be sought-after analysts. Students gain an understanding of analytic tools such as Python and R to leverage big-data insights for driving business strategy forward. The curriculum blends core business knowledge with training in Python, R, and Tableau to prepare students for high-impact roles in data analytics. Students have the option to choose between a non-internship track or an expanded internship option to gain real-world experience. The program also includes a capstone project where students apply statistical and analytical tools to real-world business problems using real data.

Satisfactory completion of the master's thesis is also required for the degree. Students who pursue the MS degree without thesis (Plan B) must earn a minimum of 30 credits of coursework acceptable for graduate credit.

Candidates for admission to the program must have earned a baccalaureate degree, or its equivalent. ProgramName: Master of Science in Clinical Nurse Leader
Requirements: Applicants must have a Bachelor's degree from an accredited school, a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 from their most recent relevant degree, an RN licensure from New York State, and one year of clinical experience. [2] A statistics course with a grade of C or above is also required. [2]
Description: The Clinical Nurse Leader program prepares nurses to understand the challenges and opportunities faced by a broad patient base and the healthcare system. [2] It focuses on putting evidence-based practice into action to enhance safety and quality. [2] The program, which includes hybrid coursework and an immersion experience/capstone project, is designed to improve patient care at the point of delivery and expand the nurse's role as a care coordinator, clinical informaticist, unit educator, program coordinator, nurse manager, or nurse executive. [2] As one of the first institutions to offer a master's degree aligned with the CNL certification, the University of Rochester's program is the only one of its kind in Upstate New York. [2] Clinical leaders who earn this master's degree work at the intersection of clinical care, population health, and healthcare management. [2]
Accredidation: The master's degree program in nursing at the University of Rochester School of Nursing is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). ProgramName: Master of Science in Dental Sciences
Requirements: While the University of Rochester does not specify a single set of institute-level application requirements, the application process for graduate school generally involves preparing materials such as personal essays, gathering letters of recommendation, and submitting transcripts. Applicants are advised to register for and take any required graduate entrance exams as specified by their individual program of interest.
Description: The Master of Science in Dental Sciences is designed to equip dental clinicians with the critical thinking skills needed to effectively apply research knowledge and techniques to enhance patient health outcomes. The program also prepares graduates to engage in research activities and pursue academic careers. [2] This master's degree is ideal for individuals who have earned a doctorate in dentistry and possess clinical training, as well as those enrolled in advanced education programs, dental clinical specialties, or junior faculty with clinical responsibilities. [2] The curriculum offers comprehensive training in the fundamental skills of clinical research, complemented by a wide range of core and elective courses. [2] These courses are structured to provide foundational concepts and theories tailored to the individual student's professional goals. [2] Each student works closely with an advisor and advisory committee to create a personalized study plan that aligns with their interests and career goals. While master's candidates generally complete all program requirements, including a written thesis and final oral examination, within 24 months, the program can extend to a 3-year timeline for those enrolled in 3-year residency programs. [2] Graduates of the Master of Science in Dental Sciences gain the expertise to lead a wide range of clinical studies, bridging the gap between scientific knowledge and clinical practice. By translating cutting-edge research into real-world applications, they enhance patient care, contribute to evidence-based practices, and drive innovation in the dental field. [2] In addition, the program prepares graduates for academic careers, equipping them with the research skills and critical thinking necessary to mentor future generations of dental professionals and conduct impactful, high-level research. [2]
Accredidation: The Postdoctoral Dental Education and Residency Training Programs at the Eastman Institute for Oral Health are accredited by the American Dental Association's Commission on Dental Accreditation and have been granted the accreditation status of approval without reporting requirements. Description: The master of science in diagnostic imaging program is a multidisciplinary program offered in partnership between the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering in Arts, Sciences & Engineering, and the Department of Imaging Sciences in the University of Rochester Medical Center. [1] Students in this program will learn both the theory and practice of medical imaging using clinical need as a guiding principle. [1] This one-year program aims to develop the next generation of medical imaging professionals by teaching students the theory and practice that underpin modern imaging systems, including emerging artificial intelligence techniques. [1] The curriculum includes core courses in signal and image processing, deep learning, and inverse problems as well as hands-on clinical classes. [1] By the end of the program, students will understand the image processing techniques used to enhance interpretability of medical images, the practical aspects of clinical imaging modalities and to recognize what aspects of imaging are most important to radiologists, and the scientific basis for understanding image formation with emphasis on solutions to inverse problems. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Education Policy
Requirements: Online application form. A non-refundable application fee ($70 for domestic students, $90 for international). Official transcripts from all prior institutions of higher education. Statement of Purpose (1-3 pages). Current resume/curriculum vitae. Applicants must have an earned B.A. or B.S. International students whose primary language is not English must also include TOEFL scores.
Description: At the Warner School of Education, our master’s degree in education policy will help you serve as a catalyst for change, preparing you to be successful in influencing and leading policy creation and implementation across diverse educational settings. [1] Warner's innovative education policy program provides students the opportunity to examine and understand contemporary policy issues impacting the educational spectrum. It delivers students the in-depth knowledge and strategic skills and tools to design, implement, and evaluate educational policies at the local, state, federal, and even international levels. [1] Students learn to apply a variety of conceptual, theoretical, and analytic frameworks - including ones from sociology, politics, economics, finance, and law – and how they can impact education policy. This ensures our graduates are well prepared to apply their deep and diverse understanding, knowledge, and skills in educational policy to support any number of research, governmental, non-profit, community, school district, and higher education organizations. [1] Warner's 30-credit master's in education policy provides an interdisciplinary program that equips students with the knowledge and tools to influence, design, implement, and/or evaluate local, state, national, and/or international policies. [1]
Accredidation: The Association for Advancing Quality in Educator Preparation (AAQEP) has awarded full seven-year accreditation to the educator preparation programs in the University of Rochester's Warner School of Education and Human Development. [2] The University of Rochester is a member in good standing of the Association for Advancing Quality in Educator Preparation (AAQEP), a national accrediting organization recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation. The programs listed below have been awarded full accreditation by AAQEP through June 30, 2031. [3]

For undergraduate admissions, the university uses the Common Application or Coalition Application and employs a holistic review process. For graduate admissions, requirements are specific to each individual program.
Description: Epidemiology is the science that studies the distribution, determinants, and patterns of disease in human populations. It is a cornerstone of public health, and informs policy decisions and evidence-based clinical practice by identifying risk factors for disease and targets for preventive healthcare. [2] Our MS in Epidemiology program in the Department of Public Health Sciences is a 34-credit course of study designed to provide students with the methodologies and skills needed to 1) carry out research and manage public health programs to identify correlates of disease that may be targets of primary prevention; 2) evaluate the consequences of changes in health care delivery on populations; and 3) to accommodate the growing need to integrate and analyze large-scale information. [2] Our MS program sits within a large urban medical center and all its clinical research resources and collaborative faculty at the University of Rochester. [2] The University is home to numerous health sciences graduate programs and a large diverse student body. [2] Students completing the program will be well prepared to take positions in academic research, private industry, government, and non-profit agencies. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester has been accredited by CEPH since 1978. [12]
ScholarshipType: Departmental financial aid may include limited tuition scholarships for qualified students, and as available, research assistantships and/or teaching assistantships.

Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree in nursing from an accredited school, a GPA of at least 3.0 in the most recent degree, and a current U.S. RN license. Additionally, a college-level statistics course with a grade of 'C' or better is required. The application process is managed through an online portal, and applicants must submit official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Family Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
Requirements: Applicants must have a Bachelor's degree in nursing from an accredited school or an equivalent master's RN license-qualifying degree in nursing. A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 from the most recent relevant degree is required. Applicants must also have RN licensure from New York State and have completed a statistics course with a grade of C or better. [4]

Accredidation: The master's degree program in nursing at the University of Rochester is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Family Therapy Training
Description: The Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy program is a three-year, 63-credit hour program that provides clinical training in the field of family therapy. Our program is rooted in a Biopsychosocial and Family Systems approach, which values the inclusion of families in health care. The program provides the educational and clinical training necessary for graduates to be eligible for licensure as a Marriage and Family Therapist in New York State, as well as membership in the American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy (AAMFT).
Accredidation: The Master's in Marriage and Family Therapy Program at the University of Rochester is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Marriage and Family Therapy Education (COAMFTE).
ScholarshipAmount: The Clark Family Scholarship provides a maximum of $5000.

Description: Finance is a lucrative, fast-moving field, and the competition is fierce. Ranked No. 2 in the US by Financial Times, the analytically rigorous, STEM-designated MS in Finance program from Simon Business School can help you gain a competitive edge. Whether you're pursuing a career in corporate finance, financial services, or risk management, Simon will give you the tools you need to succeed.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Genetic Counseling
Description: With an expanding array of genetic tests and the growing importance of genomic information in the delivery of health care, there has never been a better time to enter the field of genetic counseling. The Master of Science in Genetic Counseling (MSGC) program is a full-time program that prepares students for a career as a genetic counselor. Genetic counselors are essential players in the healthcare team and possess the unique skills and knowledge necessary to support individuals and families in understanding and adapting to the medical and psychological implications of genetic conditions. The genetic counseling training program within the University of Rochester School of Medicine & Dentistry prepares students for a range of career opportunities available to genetic counselors and to shape the future direction of the field!
Accredidation: The MSGC program at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Genetic Counseling (ACGC). [8]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Care Organization Management and Leadership
Requirements: Applicants must meet the following requirements to be eligible for the Leadership in Health Care Systems program: a bachelor's degree from an accredited school, a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 from the most recent relevant degree, one year of experience in the health care industry, and a statistics course with a grade of C or above. [1, 5]
Concentration: Health Care Organization Management and Leadership (HCM)
Description: The Leadership in Health Care Systems curriculum is broadly interdisciplinary with a focus on the “big picture” opportunities and challenges facing healthcare systems. Through hybrid coursework (a blend of in-person and online) and a hands-on capstone project, you'll sharpen your skills as a manager or leader and learn best practices to assure efficient, quality, and safe patient care delivery systems. [3] The program also includes 224 hours of mentored field placement with healthcare organizations and leaders. The Health Care Organization Management and Leadership (HCM) program was specifically designed to align with national and international health professional education reform principles. The goal of interprofessional education is to increase team learning among professionals from different backgrounds for the purpose of improving health care for individuals and populations. The distinct feature of the HCM program is core leadership knowledge. Subject matter includes formalized management tools, but goes further to emphasize leadership theory, principles, and practices. The HCM program has been developed for health professionals seeking career advancement and for professionals transitioning to a health care career from other fields.
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master's degree program in nursing, and Doctor of Nursing Practice program at the University of Rochester School of Nursing are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Humanities and Bioethics
Requirements: Candidates for admission to the program must have earned a baccalaureate degree, or its equivalent. Applicants must submit the following: The Online Application, Personal Statement (750 words maximum), one (1) sample of your own writing (can be academic, narrative, or creative writing), and Transcripts from all previous college and graduate programs. [1]

Description: The field of Health Humanities and Bioethics utilizes the perspectives and tools of humanities and arts disciplines to examine the human contexts of healthcare. [1] Following the biopsychosocial tradition of healthcare education at the University of Rochester, the program offers foundational training in this area. [1] Students engage with humanities to understand the interpersonal perspectives and sociocultural contexts of both patients and caregivers, and to cultivate skills that are directly applicable to the practice and teaching of healthcare. [1] This full-time, one-year Master of Science degree program is administered through the School of Medicine and Dentistry and is designed for students, trainees, professionals, and scholars in healthcare disciplines, humanities and social science disciplines, as well as those in a gap or bridging year. [1, 5]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Professions Education
Description: These innovative, interdisciplinary, and interprofessional programs – a collaboration of the University of Rochester Schools of Education, Nursing, and Medicine & Dentistry – offer healthcare professionals unique opportunities to leverage their clinical experience and perspectives and to gain education skills, with the ultimate goal of improving patient care. [8] Graduates of our health professions education programs emerge as aspiring and inspiring leaders. [8] They are well prepared to lead in an ever-changing healthcare environment and well positioned to succeed in ever-expanding roles and careers within traditional healthcare education and training environments, as well as in emerging healthcare delivery channels. [8] These programs are designed to prepare the best and the brightest health profession educators, leveraging state-of-the-art research and best practices at the intersection of health and education to significantly influence the future of healthcare. [8]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Health Services Research and Policy
Requirements: Our MS program in Health Services Research and Policy in the Department of Public Health Sciences is a 37-credit course of study designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills needed to conduct high quality health services and policy analysis. [5] We meet this goal by providing students with a multi-disciplinary foundation in the fundamental elements of health services research including health policy, biostatistical methods, health economics, epidemiology, psychology, and outcomes assessment. [5]
Department: School of Medicine and Dentistry, Department of Public Health Sciences
Description: Health services research is a multidisciplinary field of scientific investigation that studies how social factors, financing systems, organizational structures and processes, health technologies, and personal behaviors affect access to health care, the quality and cost of health care, and ultimately our health and well-being. [3] Health services research aims to provide timely, reliable, and continuously-improved evidence base to guide health care decisions made by clinicians, patients and families, executives and agencies, policymakers, and payers or purchasers. [3] Our MS program in Health Services Research and Policy in the Department of Public Health Sciences is a 37-credit course of study designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills needed to conduct high quality health services and policy analysis. [3] We meet this goal by providing students with a multi-disciplinary foundation in the fundamental elements of health services research including health policy, biostatistical methods, health economics, epidemiology, psychology, and outcomes assessment. [3] Students completing the program will be well prepared to take positions in a wide variety of private and public institutions engaged in health care management, health services research, or health policy work. [3]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Healthcare Data Science and AI (Online)

[1]

[2] The curriculum is designed for professionals from various backgrounds, including those already working in both in technical or clinical healthcare roles, and prepares program graduates for roles in data analytics, data science, and AI applied to the healthcare industry. [2] Students will learn: Various data science, AI, and machine learning methods and techniques applicable to deriving new insights from healthcare data. Practical aspects of accessing (including understanding its provenance) and analyzing healthcare data. How to develop data science solutions with real-world clinical/healthcare data sets in a fair, reproducible, and ethical manner. [2]

[1] Our graduates have successfully secured positions as researcher coordinators, development specialists and human services agency employees in the areas of health and human services, public health, and community development agencies, as well as roles as consultants in nontraditional learning environments. [1] In addition, many of our graduates use this as a stepping stone to continue their education, in pursuit of a diverse array of clinical and doctoral degrees. [1] Graduates can also successfully transition to clinical programs that complement the degree in human development, such as mental health counseling, social work, clinical or counseling psychology, or Applied Behavior Analysis. [1] Our master's degree programs in human development have also provided a vehicle for international students interested in becoming experts in emerging knowledge in the field to pursue a range of career paths. [1]

ProgramName: Master of Science in Immunology, Microbiology, and Immunology (BS/MS)

[1] Students in the program receive intensive, advanced training in immunology, microbiology, virology, and biotechnology, with a focus on hands-on research and practical skills. [1] These skills include critical scientific thinking, scientific communication, group dynamics, problem-solving, and data analysis, as well as instruction in drug discovery. [1] The program's goals are to reflect the interconnectivity and complexity of biomedical sciences and the increasing need for teamwork in the workforce. [1]

Choose your track, dive into analytics, and gain the skills to become the go-to expert for insights, pricing, and sales decisions in today's digital, data-driven marketplace. [2]

Description: Graduates of our MS in Marriage and Family Therapy Program leave with a depth of MFT knowledge and skill to competently practice as relational systemic professionals serving all comunities aith cutural ttunement, self-reflection, and a commitment to lifelong learning. Students entering our MS in Marriage and Family Therapy Program will be exposed to the major family therapy conceptual and clinical models. Based in the Department of Psychiatry, within the University of Rochester Medical Center, means our students are embedded in a clinical practice site/hospital vs. a college campus type setting. This setting provides the unique opportunity to learn about mental health and families in a collaborative interdisciplinary context. Students complete yearlong clinical training at two practicum sites concurrently in their second year: several Rochester community-based clinical sites complement our onsite NYS Office of Mental Health regulated clinic, Strong Family Therapy Services. Practicum students receive weekly individual and group supervision at each site from AAMFT-approved supervisors or supervisors who are equivalently trained to provide relational systemic supervision.

Description: The Master of Science in Medical Technology and Innovation is a specialized MS program in biomedical engineering offered through the Center for Medical Technology and Innovation (CMTI). [2] It provides students with hands-on experience in clinical observation and medical device design, preparing them for careers in healthcare innovation and bioengineering. [2] The program is structured to mirror the real-world innovation pipeline, beginning with a summer of clinical rotations to identify unmet clinical needs. [3] This is followed by a fall semester focused on needs filtering and concept generation, and a spring semester dedicated to design refinement, prototyping, and exploring IP, regulatory, and reimbursement strategies. [3] Students receive extensive training in the commercialization process of medical devices and become familiar with the complexities of the medical device industry, including FDA regulations, intellectual property, and quality systems. [1] Key components of the program include clinical immersion in real hospital settings, direct collaboration with surgeons, hands-on prototyping, and training in regulatory and intellectual property essentials. If your piece is electroacoustic and does not have a score, you may upload a PDF indicating this along with the recording. Composition applicants are required to upload recordings of your composed works. Note: MIDI recordings only are acceptable if acoustic recordings are not available. Research paper(s): Composition and Music Education applicants must submit one music research paper. [8] Selected composition applicants will be interviewed by the composition faculty. [9]
Description: The PhD degree in Composition is a research-oriented program that emphasizes high-level composition and scholarship. [5] The program consists of three years of coursework and includes applied composition lessons, advanced coursework in composition, theory, and history, and PhD research seminars. [3, 5] Requirements for the degree include proficiency in two foreign languages, passing comprehensive exams, and completing a two-part dissertation that consists of a large-scale composition and a research/analytical paper. [3, 5]

Requirements: A student entering graduate study in computer science should have a strong undergraduate grounding in the fundamentals of calculus and discrete mathematics, and basic knowledge of data structures, algorithms, and one or more higher-level computing programming languages. For applicants to the PhD program some undergraduate research experience is preferred. [2]
Description: Our PhD program aims to cultivate the next generation of world-class computer science researchers. Our mission is to enable you to achieve your career dreams. [10] Our graduate program was established in 1974 and has a history of 50 years of world-class research, especially in artificial intelligence/human-computer interaction, software systems, and the theory of computation. [7] We provide a collegial, interactive environment in which faculty directly mentor students. All faculty and PhD students, regardless of their area, are familiar with each other's work. This is possible only in a relatively small, close-knit department. We believe that graduate students are the heart of our research productivity, and we make them first-class department citizens. [7] Students receive an MS degree in their second year. Most students complete their PhD in 4 to 6 years. [10]

Requirements: Admission to graduate programs in the School of Arts and Sciences and Hajim School of Engineering and Applied Sciences is highly competitive. A qualified applicant needs a strong academic record, as evidenced by high grades in relevant coursework and a strong CV/resume, as well as comprehensive letters of recommendation. [13] Common application materials include a statement of purpose, letters of recommendation, transcripts, and a CV/resume. However, each program has its own specific requirements and deadlines, and applicants are advised to consult the website of the department or program to which they are applying for detailed information. [13]
Description: The goal of the doctoral program is to form scholars who will contribute to the field of economics a topnotch-notch researchers, instructors, and mentors. The program requires at least three years of full-time study. Most students remain in the program for five or six years. Our approach is to provide intensive training, both in coursework and in writing/presenting research papers. Our relatively small size, together with our collegial environment, is conducive to a tight-knit research community where graduate students are treated as research peers to faculty. The basic coursework consists of core courses in the first year, and field and distributional courses in the second year. Independent research usually begins in the third year, but often students start working on their own projects as early as the summer between years one and two. Students are required to produce a research paper by the end of the third year, a paper that is often included in their dissertation.

Barnard Fellowship. [32]

Requirements: All students must submit the following materials in the online application to be considered: a statement of purpose (two to three pages, double spaced), a writing sample, and two to three letters of recommendation, preferably from English faculty. The writing sample should be a substantial piece of work (10-20 pages, or a comparable excerpt from a longer effort) that reflects the candidate's analytical skills and writing ability. [8] While most applicants to the PhD program have a BA or MA in English, qualified students from related disciplines are also welcome. [8] The application deadline for the PhD program is January 15. [8]
Description: The National Research Council ranks the University of Rochester's Department of English among the best PhD programs in the country. Our program offers students the scholarly resources and intellectual energy of a major research institution in an environment that permits close personal attention and open exchange. Students in the department interact with a faculty of active scholars and teachers whose publications and professional engagements continue to garner national and international recognition.

Requirements: A Bachelor's degree and minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0. Official transcripts must be received from each accredited college or university attended. A minimum of three (3) letters of recommendation. Supplemental questions. Curriculum vitae (C.V.) or resume. [1]
Description: Since 2002, the PhD in Epidemiology program innovators in and highly productive epidemiologists studying of the distribution and determinants of disease in human populations, both locally and nationally/internationally. Set within a large medical center with all its clinical research resources and collaborative faculty, our doctoral program prepares students for academic careers focused on research and education in the public health and medical fields, as well as careers in private industry, government, and non-profit agencies. Our students come from around the world, and while in Rochester, live, learn, and grow in an academic environment that nurtures individuality, scientific inquiry, intellectual discussion, and personal development.

Requirements: Admission requirements include a completed online application, upload of official transcripts for all university-level coursework, official test scores for either the GMAT or GRE, three letters of recommendation, and two required essays with the option for a third. [11, 12] A business-formatted résumé is also required. [12] International applicants may also need to submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. [11]
Fees: All Simon PhD students receive a full-tuition scholarship for all courses approved for their curriculum. [2]
Description: Simon's methodological approach to finance emphasizes formal modeling of problems and empirical testing of theories. Explore topics related to areas such as corporate finance, financial institutions, and asset pricing using principles of economics, mathematics, and statistics. [3]
Accredidation: Simon Business School is accredited by AACSB. The AACSB International (The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business) accreditation represents the highest standard of achievement for business schools worldwide. [9]
ScholarshipAmount: Admitted PhD students qualify for an annual fellowship for five years of study. [2]

ProgramName: PhD in Genetics, Development and Stem Cells
Requirements: Admission is on a competitive basis. In addition to prior academic training and performance, your research aptitude, letters of reference, and personal statement will help us select the most qualified applicants. [2] Important requirements for your application include a transcript of your undergraduate training and at least three reference letters. [1] Applicants will be required to submit a current curriculum vitae. [2] Candidates that have demonstrated their interest in science, both in their course work and through seeking out research opportunities, will be given preference. A solid foundation in biochemistry, molecular and cell biology will also prepare students for our rigorous training program. [1]
Description: The primary goal of the GDSC graduate program is to provide state-of-the-art, research-intensive education for students seeking to obtain a Ph.D. degree in the study of development and disease using modern genetic approaches. [1] The program provides students with the research and teaching skills necessary to become successful and independent scientists employed in academic, government, and corporate settings. [1] Students entering graduate school through the program of Genetics, Development and Stem Cells will perform cutting-edge research on topics including organism function and development, disease models, and stem cell biology. [2] Advanced cutting-edge experimental systems in genetics, molecular biology, genomics, proteomics and computational biology are used and taught. [2] Successful completion of the graduate program culminates in the granting of the Ph.D. degree in Genetics. [1]
Accredidation: All graduate programs in the SMD are accredited per the University of Rochester's Middle States Commission on Higher Education accreditation as a graduate degree-granting institution, overseen by the Office of the Provost. [6]

ProgramName: PhD in Health Services Research and Policy
Department: Department of Public Health Sciences, School of Medicine and Dentistry
Fees: Full-time PhD students receive a full tuition scholarship.
Fees.1: Full-time PhD students receive a tuition scholarship valued at $68,800 for the 2025-2026 academic year. [16]
Description: Since 1994, the PhD program in Health Services Research and Policy in the Department of Public Health Sciences has been highly successful in preparing students to become scholars for research, teaching, and public service careers in university, public policy, and governmental settings. Our PhD program is designed to produce researchers who generate knowledge and strategies used in solving healthcare problems. Our PhD program has also been designated as a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) program since 2010. Set within a large medical center with all its clinical research resources and collaborative faculty, our program focuses on interdisciplinary application of the social and behavioral science disciplines to real world health issues such as the organization, financing, and delivery of health care; the quality and safety of care; health outcomes; and the management of population health.
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. [8, 9, 10]
ScholarshipAmount: A competitive stipend of $35,100 per year is provided for 12-month programs for the 2026-2027 academic year.
ScholarshipType: Fellowship including a tuition scholarship and a competitive stipend.

[3] Most applicants to the MA and PhD programs have the equivalent of an undergraduate degree and/or an MA in history, but the department welcomes qualified students who previously had specialized in other related disciplines and show clear promise of excellent work in history. [3] The department does not set a minimum grade point average for admission. [3] However, our experience shows that anyone with less than an overall GPA of 3.0 and a GPA of 3.5 in history courses rarely qualifies for admission. [3]

ProgramName: PhD in Immunology, Microbiology and Virology
Requirements: Application Requirements for PhD Programs include: Create an SMD Graduate Admissions Application, Statement of Purpose, Uploaded copy of transcript(s) to online application, and 3 Letters of Recommendation. The Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) is a mandatory requirement for applicants whose primary language is not English. [1]
Fees: Full tuition scholarship, including all academic fees.
Fees.1: Full tuition scholarship, including all academic fees. [4]
Description: The Immunology, Microbiology, and Virology (IMV) Program is designed for students interested in obtaining a Ph.D. in Microbiology & Immunology. [8, 11] We offer in-depth coursework and diverse research opportunities that focus on immunology, microbiology, and virology. The flexibility of our training program allows students to train in a number of exciting research areas including: cancer, autoimmune disease, respiratory pathogens and often allows students to develop highly effective interdisciplinary collaborations, resulting in cutting edge thesis projects. Housed in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology, the Immunology, Microbiology, and Virology PhD Program (IMV) houses a diverse group of faculty with expertise in bacteriology, virology, fungi, and immunology. [6, 8] Current research emphasizes cutting-edge molecular techniques and includes, but is not limited to, studies on: autoimmunity, biodefense, bioinformatics, biofilms, cancer biology, gene therapy, genetics and genomics, HIV/AIDS, immunologic mechanisms, respiratory pathogens (including influenza) and vaccine development. [6, 8]
ScholarshipAmount: A competitive stipend for 2026-2027 of $35,100 per year for 12-month programs.

Requirements: Admission requirements include upload of official transcripts, official test scores (either GRE or GMAT and TOEFL or IELTS if required), three letters of recommendation and two essays with an optional third essay. [2, 5] A strong quantitative background is essential. [2] The Simon PhD Program does not have minimum requirements for test scores or GPA. [2] As part of the online application, you will be asked to supply three recommendations. [5] We require a business formatted résumé (not a CV) and recommend it be no longer than two pages. [5] The application will provide two essay prompts, with space to upload an optional third essay. [5] School-issued official transcripts, scanned and uploaded for each college attended. [5] Please note, Simon has made the strategic decision to pause PhD admissions for Fall 2026 to strengthen and sustain the program's long-term impact. [12]
Description: Simon's PhD in Information Systems and Technology focuses on the business aspects of Information Technology use and management, and the analytic and quantitative tools and techniques to address them. [10] The research conducted by the students and faculty has significantly advanced the state of the art in research on information systems in general, with an emphasis on information systems economics and machine learning modeling. [10, 11]

Description: The interdepartmental graduate program in materials science offers a MS and PhD in materials science. [8] There are two core areas of required courses, with flexibility to allow students to choose from the course list in the Graduate Bulletin under materials science. [8] These courses are generally also cross-listed with one of twelve participating science and engineering departments. [8] At Rochester, there are more than 60 faculty spanning nearly a dozen science and engineering departments support research, academics, and entrepreneurship in materials science. [7] Plus, our collaborations with the University's nearby Medical Center, Laboratory for Laser Energetics, and Institute of Optics create unparalleled opportunities to accelerate material advances. [7]

Description: The University of Rochester department of Mathematics invites you to pursue a PhD with our well-respected faculty. The department has active research groups in: Algebra and number theory, Analysis, Combinatorics, Geometry, Probability, Ergodic Theory, Mathematical Physics, and Topology. We maintain small class sizes with a high level of interaction between students and faculty. Our graduate students also gain valuable professional experience by working with our innovative undergraduate program, including WeBWorK.

Description: Faculty research in the department falls into two broad categories: solid mechanics-materials science, and fluid mechanics-plasma physics. Much of this work is interdisciplinary and takes advantage of links between the department and the: Laboratory for Laser Energetics, Rochester Center for Biomedical Ultrasound, School of Medicine and Dentistry, Department of Physics and Astronomy, Department of Biomedical Engineering. [3] The PhD in mechanical engineering requires 90 hours of graduate credit. Students holding a master of science degree receive 30 credit hours toward the 90 required hours. Students are required to take at least 32 hours of coursework at the 400 level or higher, of which at least 24 credit hours should be mechanical engineering courses. The dissertation is typically about 30 of the total of 90 credit hours. [4]

Requirements: Applicants to the PhD in Music Education should have 2-3 years of music teaching experience. A master's degree must be earned before being admitted to the PhD program. [16, 19] General application materials include an online application, a personal statement, a résumé/CV, three letters of recommendation, and transcripts from all collegiate study. [12] Note: The university states there are no PhD openings for fall 2026, with an anticipation of reopening for fall 2027. [12, 24]

ScholarshipAmount: Scholarships range from 1-2 units to full tuition.

Requirements: Applicants for the PhD in Musicology must submit two music research papers. [14] All application materials must be submitted by the December 1st deadline for pre-screening. [5] Following this review, a limited number of applicants will be invited to an interview via Zoom. [5] General application materials for graduate programs include a CV/resume, a statement of purpose, and letters of recommendation. [2] The PhD in Musicology requires reading proficiency in two foreign languages, typically German and either French or Italian. [11] Please note: The university's website indicates there are no PhD openings for Fall 2026, with openings anticipated for Fall 2027. [14]
Description: Musicology at Eastman is intensely interdisciplinary and intimately informed by the rich musical environment of the school. The department offers a PhD degree, with an emphasis in historical and critical studies or ethnomusicology, and an MA degree in musicology or ethnomusicology. [2] With eight full-time faculty plus affiliated faculty at the University of Rochester, the Musicology Department features expertise in subjects ranging from opera, jazz, and Renaissance sacred music to gender studies, ecomusicology, and intersections between music and politics. [2] The Musicology Department provides students across the Eastman community with creatively designed courses that explore the intricacies of musical meaning and aesthetics in widely divergent historical, cultural, and geographical settings. Undergraduates learn to think critically about the history of music in courses that blend temporal breadth with topical focus, while graduate students receive broad training in a range of musical traditions and critical methodologies. [2]
Accredidation: The PhD in Musicology program at the University of Rochester is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [3, 15]

Requirements: Applicants must have earned a U.S. baccalaureate degree or its equivalent from a college, university, or technical school of acceptable standing. Students entering the program typically have a baccalaureate degree in one of the natural or applied sciences (e.g., Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Physics, Neuroscience, Psychology, Biomedical Engineering). Successful applicants will usually have had college-level coursework, or equivalent professional experience, in disciplines relevant for neuroscience, including the biological sciences, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. In addition, prior laboratory research experience is strongly recommended. [2]
Fees.1: All students admitted to the PhD in Neuroscience program receive a full tuition scholarship. [6] For the 2026-2027 academic year, admitted students also receive a competitive stipend of $35,100 per year. [6] A second grade below a B- is grounds for dismissal from the PhD program. [4]
Description: The Neuroscience Graduate Program at the University of Rochester offers an outstanding opportunity for graduate training in an exceptionally interactive and collaborative environment at a world class research institution. Our mission is to prepare the next generation of creative, independent neuroscientists through academic instruction, research experience, and active mentoring. The program brings together faculty with a broad range of expertise from departments and centers across the School of Medicine and the adjacent School of Arts, Sciences, and Engineering. Research interests span all major themes in contemporary neuroscience—from cellular to systems-level studies, basic science to translational approaches—utilizing state-of-the-art techniques. A trademark of our program is the vast collaboration within and across these themes, allowing students to design thesis projects without traditional boundaries. Students are encouraged to develop expertise in their chosen subject while maintaining a strong general background in neuroscience through coursework and interactions with faculty and peers. [6]
ScholarshipAmount: $35,100 per year stipend for 2026-2027
ScholarshipType: Full tuition scholarship and annual stipend

The Graduate Admissions Committee considers many factors in their decision: GPA, GRE, TOEFL/IELTS scores, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, classes taken, and grades of those classes. Minimum undergraduate GPA is 3.0 out of 4.0. [2]

Description: The PhD program in optics prepares students for high-level research in academia, industry, or national laboratories. [2] Students are exposed to a broad range of areas within this field through class work, seminars, and one-on-one meetings with faculty. [2] The doctoral program is designed to prepare its graduates to carry out independent, creative research in an industrial, academic, or government settings. [15] Admission to the optics PhD program is very competitive, with approximately 12 to 15 students admitted each year. [15]
CostPerCredit: $2,150 per credit hour for the 2025-26 academic year, however, PhD students typically receive tuition coverage. [21]
ScholarshipType: Tuition discounts and fellowships are available. [13]

Ideal candidates will have previous laboratory research experience with a minimum overall grade point average of at least 3.0. A Statement of Purpose, copy of transcript(s) from all post-secondary institutions attended, a resume or curriculum vitae, and three (3) Letters of Recommendation are required. [5]
Fees.1: All students receive a full-tuition scholarship.
Description: The PhD Program in Pathology trains students to understand the cell biological basis for human disease and leverage those discoveries for better diagnosis and treatment options. The program is multidisciplinary in nature, drawing on faculty expertise in all aspects of disease biology including: defining molecular mechanisms underlying human disease; developing model systems, from genetic models to human tissue studies; big data and 'omic' sciences (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, lipidomics, metabolomics, and microbiomics); and designing therapeutic interventions using regenerative biology, forward pharmacology, and rational drug design. Students work with any faculty throughout the University of Rochester Medical Center whose research focuses on cell biological mechanisms of pathogenesis. Graduates go on to diverse and rewarding careers in academic, medical, industrial, non-profit, and governmental settings.
ScholarshipType: Full-tuition scholarship, paid individual health insurance, and an annual stipend

Requirements: Applications must include: A writing sample. This can include your work from undergraduate courses in philosophy. Transcripts. Unofficial transcripts are accepted, but official transcripts will be required upon admittance to the university. Three confidential letters of recommendation. A personal statement addressing a specific set of questions. A list of completed philosophy courses. [2]
Fees: All of our PhD students receive a comprehensive program of financial aid, including fellowships and appointments in teaching. As of Fall 2023, the packages cover six years. All fellowship awards provide a nine-month stipend and cover the entire cost of tuition as well as health insurance and access to the Columbia Student Health Service. [1]
Fees.1: The tuition for the PhD in Philosophy program is fully covered by the financial aid package provided to all admitted students. [1]
Description: The PhD program is at the center of intellectual life in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Rochester. The program is small (approximately 10 full-time faculty and 33 pHd students) and PhD students work closely with faculty. [2] In addition to graduate seminars, there are usually a number of reading groups each semester, and a great deal of the PhD curriculum involves independent work with faculty. [2] PhD students also serve as Teaching Assistants (TAs), and have opportunities to teach their own courses. The department maintains an active colloquium series, and the graduate students host a biennial Epistemology Conference. [2] The requirements for the PhD include 90 credits of course work and a dissertation in philosophy, and it is designed to be completed in 5 years. [2] The program will prepare students to carry out independent, creative research and scholarship in philosophy. [10] Students will demonstrate comprehensive, in-depth understanding, knowledge, and capacity for original inquiry and scholarship in primary and secondary areas of specialization chosen by the student in consultation with an advisor. [10]
CostPerCredit: $2,150 per credit hour for the 2025-26 academic year. [19]

Requirements: Students are considered for admission into the PhD program in the Department of Physics and Astronomy after completing an online application. Scanned in copies of all transcripts from university-level work (undergraduate and graduate) are required with the online application. We require at least three letters of recommendation from people who can comment on your potential for graduate study. [19] The application fee is $70. [19] We do not have a minimum GPA required for application submission. [19]

Description: The mission of the University of Rochester Department of Physics and Astronomy is to actively engage in meaningful ways to explore, understand and predict the behavior of the physical world around us, including everything from subatomic particles to the large-scale structure and evolution of the universe itself. [2] The physics and astronomy PhD program typically takes five to seven years to complete and includes coursework, preliminary assessment and qualifying examinations, teaching, research, and a dissertation. [7] Each student is required to complete at least eight advanced four credit-hour courses within the department, with at least two forming an advanced sequence in a specific field. [7] After finishing formal courses, students engage in full-time research and must register for 12 units of PhD Research in Physics/Astrophysics each semester until they reach the 90-credit limit. [7]

The Department of Physics and Astronomy offers both master's and doctoral programs with a full range of graduate-level courses and research opportunities in astronomy, biophysics, condensed matter physics, cosmology, elementary particle physics, and quantum information. [1] In addition to a Physics track and an Astrophysics track, the department offers a Chemical Physics track and a Physics Education track. [1] Our students also pursue research in related departments, such as biomedical engineering, electrical engineering, and mathematics. [1]

Description: The Department of Political Science offers a program of study leading to the degree of doctor of philosophy that is designed to train scholars who will contribute to the future development of political science through careers in teaching and research. [2] Unlike the traditional program, which is organized as a smorgasbord of offerings, the core of the Rochester program is a focused course of training that covers all of the technical tools of contemporary political science. [2] Each student receives training in one or more substantive areas, including American politics, comparative politics, international relations, or political philosophy, but every one of them attains a degree of sophistication in formal theory and statistical methods that is rarely achieved by graduates of more traditional programs. [2] The PhD program at Rochester is unique. It is the most rigorous training program available within a department of political science anywhere in the world. [2]

Description: The department offers a Ph.D. in Psychology, in which students specialize one of five core training areas. Students are trained with a strong foundation in theory, research methods and advanced statistics, as well as in classic and contemporary issues relevant to their specific area. Students collaborate with faculty on research from the very beginning of their graduate training and are encouraged to gain research experience with more than one faculty member. As student's interests and skills develop, they pursue more independent research projects.

Official English language test scores for international applicants. [15]

Description: The Ph. D. in Statistics with Concentration in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology is designed to educate the next generation of biostatisticians with the knowledge required to address critical scientific and public health questions. [10] The Department of Biostatistics and Computational Biology at the University of Rochester is home to one of the few Statistics graduate programs nationwide that offers a medical school location with an academic research focus. [10] This easy access to clinical and translational collaborations provides many opportunities for stimulating interaction with applied research, especially when compared to peer programs housed in Schools of Arts and Sciences (Statistics) or Public Health (Biostatistics). [10] The department conducts teaching and research in statistical theory and methodology oriented toward the health sciences. [10] The department interprets the term "statistics" very broadly, with specialization available in probability, statistical theory and analysis, biostatistics, and interdisciplinary areas of application. Description: The PhD Program in Translational Biomedical Science is focused on creating a new kind of investigator—one who has a much broader view. A flexible curriculum in basic, translational and population health sciences and a dual mentoring approach for dissertation research make it a uniquely powerful way to prepare the research leaders of tomorrow. [2] The goal of this exciting new program is to prepare individuals for investigative and clinical careers relating to the translation of basic biomedical research into clinical strategies to improve health, and to stimulate targeting of basic scientific research towards pursuit of mechanisms and causes of and optimal therapies to prevent and cure human disease. [9] To improve human health, fundamental scientific discoveries and critically evaluated clinical observations must be translated into practical clinical applications. [9] Important discoveries from “the bench” of basic biomedical research performed at the molecular or cellular level must progress to the clinical level, to the “bedside.” Key observations at “the bedside” stimulate scientists to examine pathophysiologic phenomena and to devise new approaches to elucidate disease mechanisms and therapeutic approaches based on such demonstrated causes. Description: Anthropology is the study of humankind. It is a diverse and holistic field that uses four interconnected approaches to understand the human condition: cultural anthropology, archaeology, linguistic anthropology, and biological anthropology. At Rochester, the Department of Anthropology is a vibrant intellectual community of scholars and students dedicated to understanding the social and cultural worlds people create, as well as the biological and evolutionary history of our species. The undergraduate program in anthropology is designed to introduce students to the breadth of the discipline while allowing them to focus on areas of particular interest. Students are encouraged to develop their own research projects, often in collaboration with faculty members, and to gain hands-on experience through fieldwork, internships, and study abroad programs. The department prides itself on its commitment to undergraduate education, offering small classes, close faculty-student interaction, and a supportive environment for learning and discovery.

Understand the frameworks in which individual moral decisions should be made. Understand the frameworks in which social and political moral decisions should be made. The flexible curriculum is designed to provide a solid foundation in the sciences, while also allowing students the intellectual freedom to explore their interests. Small class sizes and a low student-to-faculty ratio enable our world-renowned faculty to take a personalized approach to teaching. Students have the opportunity to participate in research, and many do. The University is a tier-one research institution, and the Department of Biology is one of the most active research departments on campus. Most students get involved in research by volunteering, but some also earn course credit or receive funding to conduct their own research projects.

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Required supporting materials include a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a school report/counselor recommendation, and a supplemental essay.
