Description: How a person recognizes a sound, learns their native language, what the brain does as we listen to speech, and how we remember events from the past are all questions that are studied as part of brain and cognitive sciences. [7] At the University of Rochester, the major provides students with a rigorous but accessible program if they are interested in the brain and how it allows us to perceive, think, and learn. [7] Both the Bachelor of Arts (BA) and the Bachelor of Science (BS) degrees are centered around a curriculum that integrates biological, behavioral, and computational approaches to the study of perception, language, thinking, learning, and the development of these abilities. [7] The BS program, in particular, delivers a stringent natural science education that readies students for postgraduate studies in brain and cognitive sciences and associated fields like cognitive science, cognitive neuroscience, and computational modeling. [2] In addition to courses in brain and cognitive sciences (BCS), the curriculum includes a foundation in mathematics, biology, computer programming, and symbolic systems. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition for College Application, a URochester-specific supplemental essay, a school report, counselor recommendation, and one teacher recommendation. [7, 11] The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering curriculum is built on a foundation in mathematics, chemistry, and physics. [3, 4] Required foundational courses include sequences in chemistry (Chemical Concepts, Organic Chemistry), mathematics (Calculus, Linear Algebra & Differential Equations), and physics (Mechanics, Electricity & Magnetism). [4]
Department: Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences
Fees: Tuition for the 2024-2025 academic year is $65,870. The university has not yet released tuition and fee schedules for the 2026-2027 academic year.
Description: The University of Rochester's bachelor's degree in chemical engineering combines mathematics, chemistry, physics and biology with fundamental engineering analysis and design principles. The curriculum includes the study of applied mathematics, material and energy balances, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, energy and mass transfer, separation processes, chemical reaction kinetics and reactor design, chemical process analysis, process design and simulation, and process control. [2] Courses are built on a foundation in mathematics, chemistry, and physics. [2] Students learn how to program complex process simulations and gain hands-on laboratory experiences throughout their education. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester's chemical engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of (ABET). [2, 3]
CostPerCredit: For part-time undergraduate students, the cost per credit hour for the 2024-2025 academic year is $2,058.
ScholarshipType: The University of Rochester offers both merit-based and need-based scholarships.

Requirements: To be admitted to the Minor in Chemical Engineering, students must have completed MATH 130 Calculus I, MATH 131 Calculus II, MATH 230 Calculus III, MATH 235 Mathematics for Engineering Analysis (or an equivalent combination of ordinary differential equations and linear algebra), CHEM 100 College Chemistry I, CHEM 101 College Chemistry II, and PHYS 220 Introductory Mechanics (or an equivalent calculus-based Physics I). A minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 in these specific courses is required for admission. Admission also requires the approval of the Chemical Engineering Department Head. Students who are currently in the Chemical Engineering major and decide to switch out of it are automatically eligible for the minor. [2]
Description: The objective of the minor is to provide students with core technical proficiency in chemical or environmental engineering analysis. These programs involve a coherent sequence of classes consisting of 16 credits. [4]

Requirements: Required materials for undergraduate admission include the Common Application or Coalition/Scoir Application, a high school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and a school counselor report and recommendation. [2] The university also requires applicants to complete the URochester-specific questions, which includes a supplemental essay. [2]

A minor in chemistry is a program of six chemistry courses chosen by the student in consultation with a faculty advisor from the Department of Chemistry. All of the courses should total at least 24 credit-hours in chemistry. Prerequisites for advanced courses, such as mathematics and physics prerequisites for courses in physical chemistry, must be taken in addition to the six required chemistry courses. [16]
Fees: Tuition for the minor is included in the general undergraduate tuition. There are no specific fees for the minor itself.
Description: A minor in chemistry consists of a minimum of six, four-credit courses in chemistry, beyond the prerequisites. Prerequisites for advanced courses, such as mathematics and physics prerequisites for courses in physical chemistry, must be taken in addition to the six required chemistry courses. All of the courses should total at least 24 credit-hours in chemistry. Two courses with substantial overlap of content should not be included in a program. In addition, no major and minor may overlap by more than two courses; no two minors may overlap by more than two courses.

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Common Application, a personal essay (which serves as a statement of purpose), official high school transcript, a teacher recommendation, and a counselor recommendation. The University of Rochester has a test-optional policy, so applicants can choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores. There are no minimum required scores for those who choose to submit them.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Civilization
Requirements: Application requirements are not listed on the program-specific page. General first-year application materials are submitted via the Common Application or Coalition for College Application, which includes standard sections for activities and a personal essay. Applicants must also answer University of Rochester-specific questions. [2]
Description: The ancient civilizations of Greece and Rome have influenced all successive western societies, leaving a legacy that includes ideas about democracy, empire, myth, society, race, gender, and philosophy. For students who want to focus on the study of the history, culture, and literature of ancient Greece and Rome, we suggest that you begin with the 100-level course that is of interest to you. [1]

Requirements: Application requirements for the Bachelor of Arts in Classics are the same as the general first-year application requirements for the University of Rochester. These include the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a school report/counselor recommendation, two teacher recommendations, and a personal essay. The University of Rochester has a test-optional policy, so applicants can choose whether or not to submit SAT or ACT scores.
Description: The classics major is language centered, emphasizing ancient history, art and archaeology, literature, and philosophy. [3] Students in this major will learn to analyze and interpret significant texts in the ancient languages and to understand their cultural context. [24] Students study the foundational texts and significant artifacts of the western world in order to understand them on their own terms and in their ancient contexts as well as to develop a deeper awareness of the ways in which classical antiquity has shaped and continues to influence contemporary society. [2, 3] The department offers bachelor of arts degrees in religion, in classics, and in classical civilization, as well as minors in religion, classics, Latin, Greek, Hebrew and Arabic. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is an accredited institution and a member of the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [18] The University's academic programs are registered with the New York State Education Department (NYSED). [18] No specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Arts in Classics program is mentioned.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Literature
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. The application includes a personal essay. Applicants must also provide an official high school transcript, a school report, a counselor recommendation, and one teacher recommendation. An optional second teacher recommendation may also be submitted.
Concentration: ['Track one focuses the study of two or more national literatures and cultures in relation to each other.', 'Track two reflects on theoretical concepts and with questions that span literary study more generally (genre, form, etc.). It requires students to concentrate on at least one non-English language national literature alongside cultural and critical theory courses.']
Description: Comparative literature is the critical, interdisciplinary study of literature, other media, and cultures from different geographic regions, linguistic groups, and historical periods. In the broadest sense, it provides the tools to compare and contrast peoples' experiences, identities, and material products in various places and times. Central to comparative literature is how literature, culture, and media are theorized and studied across historical periods, and how they inform and influence each other. [2] Sensitive to how different geographic regions and linguistic groups conceive their identities in an era of globalization, students of comparative literature aim to increase international awareness through humanistic inquiry. [2] In light of this increasingly global outlook, translation studies are an important aspect of comparative literature, which asks questions like: What does it mean to translate texts, ideas, and perspectives across linguistic, ethnic, and national boundaries? What happens to those texts, ideas, and perspectives in such a process? [2] Students in comparative literature are, by definition, proficient in more than one language. They work in various fields adjacent to literature, such as film, music, the visual arts, philosophy, history, and anthropology. Those who study comparative literature acquire valuable skills in literary analysis, cultural awareness, critical thinking, verbal and written communication, and argumentation. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science
Requirements: To apply, you'll need to submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a teacher recommendation, and a school counselor recommendation. A mid-year report with senior year grades is also required. There is an optional writing supplement that allows you to submit a piece of analytical or creative writing. While not required, you can also submit a resume detailing your extracurricular activities.
Description: Our flexible BA program allows students to build a strong foundation in computer science while exploring other academic interests, preparing them for careers that combine computing with fields like business, design, cognitive science, and beyond. [18]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: At the University of Rochester, admission and scholarship consideration for Arts, Sciences & Engineering are based on a holistic review process that includes many academic and non-academic indicators. [4]
Description: The BS program provides rigorous preparation in all core areas of computer science and is for students interested in cutting-edge research and development careers in industry or academia. Our courses give students a solid and rigorous background in computer science principles, including the requisite mathematical foundations, while exposing them to the problems and solution techniques used in a wide range of disciplines. Students in the BS program gain deep technical expertise and hands-on experience in advanced computing topics, preparing them for careers in software engineering, research, and graduate study in computer science and related fields.

Requirements: To declare a minor in computer science, current students must first have an officially declared major. [5, 8] They should consult the department's website and discuss their plans with an authorized faculty member. [5, 8] Once the advisor approves the plan, the student can submit the online Major/Minor Declaration Form. [5, 9] The course requirements for the minor are to complete six (6) four-credit computer science courses above the level of 130. [2]
Description: Our computer science minor strengthens your ability to analyze problems, work with data, and create technology-driven solutions. With courses ranging from programming and machine learning to mobile apps and graphics, you'll gain practical skills that complement nearly any major. [2]

Requirements: To declare a minor in dance, students must be enrolled at the University of Rochester. The process involves completing a minor declaration form and meeting with a faculty advisor. The minor requires the completion of 26 credit hours in designated dance and movement studies courses.
Description: Our dance minor develops skills in observation, analysis, and critical response to dance as an art form and as a component of life and culture. [4] We do not merely dance for the sake of fitness or memorizing steps, as our studies are the result of theoretically based movement explorations and more. [4] Students in this minor will learn dance literacy and appreciation. [4] They can also get hands-on experience in: Performance; Teaching; Arts management; Choreography; Criticism; Production design. [4] Regardless of an individual student's career path, a minor in dance helps foster educated audiences and participants in the diverse field of dance in culture. [4]
ScholarshipAmount: The merit-based scholarships are awarded to International students for academic excellence. The University of Rochester scholarships that are based on merit range from $2,000 per year to full tuition fee coverage. [23]

Requirements: The Digital Media Studies (DMS) minor consists of six courses. [7] Students can choose to have the minor in either the humanities or the natural sciences division. [7] For the humanities track, students must take DMST 101, DMST 103, and four other approved humanities courses. For the natural sciences track, students must take DMST 101, either DMST 102 or CSC 161, three other approved natural science courses, and one approved humanities course. [7] Students are not required to complete all introductory courses before declaring the minor. [9] Declaration of the minor follows the standard university process for sophomores. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies
Requirements: To apply as a first-year student, applicants must use either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. The required materials include the application itself with URochester-specific questions and a supplemental essay, a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a school report with a counselor recommendation, and a mid-year report when it becomes available. [2, 6] For international applicants, there may be additional requirements such as proof of English proficiency. [4]
Description: The East Asian studies (EST) program is an interdisciplinary approach to the languages, history, and culture of this important part of the world. [2] EST majors and minors can meet the requirements for either a humanities or social science division, depending on the student's course choices. [2] Students majoring or minoring in EST must take classes from at least three departments to achieve a broad and deep understanding of East Asia. [2] The different departments at the University of Rochester that currently offer EST-relevant courses are: Art and art history; Anthropology; History; Modern languages and cultures; and Religion and classics. [2] The East Asian Studies major consists of ten courses. [2] Students must also declare a primary cultural concentration in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean. [1]

Requirements: First-year applicants can apply using the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Required materials include the application, an official high school transcript, a recommendation from one teacher, and a school report/counselor recommendation. An application fee is also required, though fee waivers are available.
Description: The undergraduate program in economics emphasizes understanding modern tools of economic analysis and their application to contemporary policy issues. The department offers a BA in economics, a BA in financial economics, as well as minors in both. For students seeking more rigorous training, there is an honors degree option in economics. In recognition of the program's high-quality, analytic approach, the University of Rochester's undergraduate Economics and Financial Economics programs, including the Honors program, have earned STEM designation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering
Requirements: For undergraduate admission to the Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences, which includes the Bachelor of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering, applicants must apply as first-year students using either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. The general application requirements for the University of Rochester apply.
Department: Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Athletic, Field-Specific, Identity-based, Community service, Military-affiliated, Employer-sponsored

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Engineering Science
Requirements: First-year applicants must apply using either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. This includes submitting the application form, a personal essay, and other standard components of these applications.
Department: School of Arts & Sciences, Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences
Concentration: While the program allows students to specialize in one or more areas through electives, which they refer to as 'Focus Areas', it does not list predefined, formal concentration names. [2]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Engineering Science (BA-ES) is a multidisciplinary program that emphasizes the understanding and application of engineering, scientific, and mathematical principles. [2, 10, 18] It provides a broad foundation in the sciences and mathematics that form the basis of engineering. [2, 10] The program allows students to gain in-depth knowledge in an area of their choice through technical electives. [2, 10] BA-ES is designed to create a solid foundation for students interested in careers such as patent attorney, technical writer, science advisor, technical sales, and science and engineering education. [2, 10]
Accredidation: The engineering science major is not ABET-accredited. [2, 10]

Requirements: First-year applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Required materials include the application itself, a supplemental essay, a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a school report/counselor recommendation, and a mid-year report. A final transcript is required upon enrollment. There is a $50 application fee, though fee waivers are available. [8, 10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Health
Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Humanities
Requirements: The University of Rochester Environmental Humanities Program does not offer a formal major for direct application. Students must first be admitted to the university through the standard undergraduate admissions process and can then propose an interdepartmental major in Environmental Humanities. [25] General application requirements for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition Application, the URochester-specific supplemental essay, an official high school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and a school report/counselor recommendation. [3, 7]
Description: The University of Rochester does not offer a Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Humanities. The Environmental Humanities Program does not yet offer a major. As of fall 2024, the minor in environmental humanities has been suspended and will no longer be offered. A cluster in Sustainability and the Environmental Humanities is available. [10, 13, 14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science
Requirements: The major in Environmental Science focuses on the interaction between Earth's physical environment and the biosphere, on anthropogenic processes like pollution and global climate change, and on environmental remediation. The program is designed to provide students with a solid background in related science fields, then delve into particular fields in environmental science in greater depth. [1]
Description: The BS in environmental science provides students with a strong foundation in the natural sciences and mathematics, and a broad background in earth sciences. The program also helps students develop strong analytical, quantitative, and communication skills needed to solve problems related to Earth systems and resources. Students in our program acquire knowledge and skills for graduate research in a variety of fields (e.g., hydrology, geochemistry, oceanography, environmental geophysics, and atmospheric science) and careers in environmental and geological consulting, environmental law, or governmental advising. [4]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is an accredited institution by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [15] Specific accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science program is not mentioned on the university's website.

Requirements: Information regarding the specific process and requirements to formally declare a Minor in Environmental Science is not available on the University of Rochester's website. Minors are generally declared by currently enrolled students, and the process typically involves consulting with a faculty advisor and submitting a form to the registrar's office. The program is interdisciplinary and designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of environmental challenges.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media Studies
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students are managed through the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. This includes a personal essay, information about extracurricular activities, and recommendations.

ProgramName: Minor in Film and Media Studies
Bachelor of Arts in Financial Economics
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, a School Report and Counselor Recommendation, at least one Teacher Recommendation, an official high school transcript, and a college essay or writing sample. The application fee is $50, though fee waivers are available. The University of Rochester is a test-optional institution, so applicants can choose whether or not to include SAT or ACT scores with their application.
Description: The undergraduate program emphasizes the understanding of modern tools of economic analysis and their application to contemporary policy issues. The University of Rochester offers a BA and a minor in economics or financial economics. Students seeking more rigorous training have the opportunity to pursue an honors degree in economics. In recognition of our high quality, analytic approach, the University of Rochester undergraduate Economics and Financial Economics programs (including Honors) have earned STEM Designation. With the BA in Economics or Financial Economics, international students in the United States on F-1 visas are eligible to work for three years in the US. Graduates of all three programs are prepared for: positions in business and government; applying to graduate programs in fields like business, law and economics; and work in economics or public policy. [14]

The French program at Rochester offers a variety of courses in language, literature, and culture. We strongly encourage our students to study in France, and we offer a semester-long program in Rennes that is particularly well-suited for majors and minors. Students can also get involved in the life of the program by coming to the weekly French-language table for lunch, by applying to live in the French-speaking section of the Modern Languages and Cultures House, and by participating in the other cultural activities that the program organizes on campus.

Requirements: The minor in French requires five courses beyond first-year French. These will include the core courses: FREN 153: Intermediate French, FREN 200: Advanced French, FREN 202: Introduction to French Literature, and FREN 204: Contemporary France. The fifth course is an elective, which must be a 200-level course taught in French.
Description: The minor in French requires five courses beyond first-year French. These will include the core courses: FREN 153: Intermediate French, FREN 200: Advanced French, FREN 202: Introduction to French Literature, and FREN 204: Contemporary France. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender, Sexuality, and Women's Studies
Description: Gender, sexuality, and women's studies focuses on the experiences of diverse groups of individuals and analyzes the changing cultural, economic, political, and psychological relationships among them. [4] Because we ask questions about gender and sexuality that no single academic department is able to answer, we encourage an interdisciplinary approach to research and learning. [4] Every semester over 300 undergraduate students from across the University enroll in gender, sexuality, and women's studies courses. [4] To complete a major, a student must take 10 courses (40 credits) in GSWS. [2] Students may use up to 4 courses taken abroad to complete their GSW major. [2]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [14] This institutional accreditation has been in place since 1921 and was most recently reaffirmed in 2024. [14, 15] There is no mention of a specific programmatic accreditation for the Bachelor of Arts in Gender, Sexuality, and Women's Studies.

ProgramName: Minor in Gender, Sexuality, and Women's Studies
Requirements: To declare a minor in Gender, Sexuality, and Women's Studies at the University of Rochester, there is no formal application process that requires documents like a resume or statement of purpose. The process involves filling out an online form available through the university's academic portal for current students. Students are also encouraged to meet with a program advisor to discuss their course plan. The main requirements are being an enrolled undergraduate student and completing the necessary declaration form.
Fees: Tuition for the 2024-2025 academic year is $65,008. Fees for 2026-2027 have not been published.

Requirements: Application requirements are not specified on the program's page. General first-year application requirements for the University of Rochester apply. These include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a personal essay (as part of the application), high school transcript, and a counselor recommendation. The university has a test-optional policy, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not required.
Description: A four-year program in geomechanics is offered jointly with the Department of Mechanical Engineering for students interested in the application of mechanics to problems associated with the atmosphere, rivers, lakes and oceans, and the earth. [3]

Requirements: Application requirements are the same for all undergraduate programs at the University of Rochester and do not vary by major. The university utilizes a holistic review process. Application materials include: a completed Common Application or Coalition Application, an official school transcript, a teacher recommendation, and a school counselor recommendation. A mid-year report is also required, and a final transcript must be sent upon graduation.
Description: German is the first language of about 120 million people in Austria, Germany, Liechtenstein, and Switzerland. It is also spoken by minorities in France, Italy, Luxemburg, the Czech Republic, Belgium, and Russia. Germany's strong economic position has also led to the use of German as the preferred language of commerce in a number of Eastern European countries. At the University of Rochester, students immerse themselves in the German language and culture through coursework, film screenings, literature, Plauderstunden (conversation hours), study abroad, and more. The program prepares students for careers that emphasize critical thinking and cross-cultural communication. Many students choose to double major in German, with combinations including Linguistics, English, Mathematics, Art History, Film, Music, History, Political Science, Optics, Psychology, Comparative Literature, International Relations, and Biomedical Engineering. Graduates have pursued careers in international business, as well as further education in medical school, graduate programs, and law school. [22]
ScholarshipType: Need-based grants, merit-based scholarships, federal and state grants, and student employment.

Requirements: The German minor has a total of 5 required courses: GRMN 151: Intermediate German I, GRMN 152: Intermediate German II, GRMN 200: Composition and Conversation, GRMN 202: Introduction to German Cultural Studies, GRMN 203: Introduction to German Literature. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Health, Behavior, and Society
Requirements: Application requirements for this program are the general first-year application requirements for the University of Rochester. Specific documents like a resume or statement of purpose are not required for general first-year admission.

ProgramName: Minor in Health, Behavior, and Society
Requirements: The Health, Behavior, and Society minor comprises six courses and fulfills the social sciences academic division of the Rochester Curriculum. The required course is PHLT 101: Introduction to Public Health I, with the remaining courses being selected from a list of approved electives. [3]

The general application requirements for first-year applicants to the University of Rochester include the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application, a URochester-specific supplemental essay, a $50 application fee (waivers are available), an official secondary school transcript, and one teacher recommendation. [9]
Description: The Department of History offers programs of study leading to a BA degree and a BA degree with honors. The department also offers a minor in history. The department offers a wide range of courses in its undergraduate program that encompass social, economic, cultural, intellectual, political, and psychological approaches to historical problems and periods. Most 100- and 200-level courses are accessible to students with little prior knowledge of history. In addition, faculty members offer 300-level seminars that explore more specialized historical problems. The history concentration is valuable for those pursuing careers in fields such as law, business, museums and archives, civil service, journalism, politics, and teaching. [1]

Requirements: Declaring a minor in history is for students already enrolled at the University of Rochester. The process involves meeting with a faculty advisor to discuss the proposed program of study and filling out a minor planning worksheet, which both the student and advisor must sign. [2] After the planning worksheet is approved by the director of undergraduate studies, the student can complete the electronic declaration form online. [2] The minor consists of six courses (24 credit hours). [9] Students cannot declare a minor until they have an officially declared major. [10]
Description: The minor in history consists of six courses (or 24 credit hours): A minimum of one course from at least two different geographical areas: Africa. Asia and the Pacific. Europe. Latin America. The Middle East. North America. A minimum of six courses (or 24 credit hours) must be taken from department faculty; no more than two courses (or 8 crc redit hours) taken outside the department can be counted toward the minor. This includes transfer courses, study abroad courses, and cross-listed courses taught by faculty not formally associated with the Department of History.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdepartmental Studies
Requirements: An interdepartmental major must consist of ten core courses (40 credits) from at least two departments, and up to four supplementary courses. The major is supervised by two faculty advisors, and is approved by the Committee on Individualized Interdepartmental Programs (CIIP). All applications must include a completed interdepartmental proposal form, proposal essays, and completed recommendation forms from faculty advisor(s). [16]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Relations
Requirements: Application requirements for first-year students at the University of Rochester are managed centrally and are not specific to the Bachelor of Arts in International Relations program. All applicants must submit the Common Application or the Coalition Application, which includes a personal essay. Other required materials include an official high school transcript, a school report, a counselor recommendation, and one teacher recommendation. The university has a test-optional policy, meaning SAT or ACT scores are not required for most applicants.

Description: The Japanese major offers students the opportunity to develop a comprehensive understanding of Japan through a combination of culture and language coursework. The Japanese major requires a total of ten courses (of at least 6.0 and/or 4.0 credits) beyond JPNS 101-102, including two Foundation Courses, four Core Language Courses, and four additional electives (language or culture). [16] There are two possible tracks for students pursuing a Japanese major: Language (8 language and 3 culture courses) and Culture (6 language and 5 culture courses). [13]

The Japanese minor consists of a total of five courses (of at least 6.0 and/or 4.0 credits) in Japanese language and culture to be selected in consultation with your undergraduate advisor. [3] This minor gives you language and cultural experience that will deepen your insights, enhance your intellectual versatility, and set you apart. [3] The Japanese Program provides unique opportunities to powerfully engage the Asian Century no matter what your field of expertise. [3] One pair of two-credit courses (e.g., Conversational Japanese, Calligraphy, etc.) may be substituted for one 4-credit course requirement for the minor. [3] Two-credit courses include JPNS 114, 115, 203, 204, 235. [3] Up to one course (language and/or culture) per semester of education abroad in Japan can be applied toward a minor in Japanese. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Jazz Studies and Contemporary Media
Requirements: Undergraduates in the School of Arts & Sciences and the Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences can declare one or more minors. Students should review the department's online offerings to understand the courses needed. They must then schedule an appointment with the departmental minor advisor to finalize their plans and gain acceptance. A Major/Minor Declaration Form must be used to declare the minor, which can only be done after a student has been accepted into a major. [6]

Fees: $69,030 per year for the 2025-2026 academic year for the School of Arts & Sciences and Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences. [27]
Description: The undergraduate Jewish studies program at University of Rochester is designed to enable students to familiarize with the history, religion, philosophy, literatures, languages and politics of Judaism. Currently, the Program offers two minors, a variety of clusters, opportunities outside the classroom, and the possibility to study abroad. Students of all backgrounds are welcome to take Jewish Studies courses and participate in the Program. Jewish civilization developed across a variety of geographical and cultural areas of the world and over thousands of years. The Program reflects these complex, many-faceted and heterogeneous dimensions of the Jewish experience, with classes on the Hebrew Bible, ancient, medieval and modern Jewish history, the Holocaust, Gender Studies, American Judaism, modern Jewish literatures, and classical and modern Hebrew. The Jewish studies minor is structured so that students have considerable independence in shaping their path of study. This allows students to focus on those areas of Judaism that are of greatest interest to them, while also developing a strong foundation in the study of Judaism and a mastery of the methods and theories used by scholars to understand Judaism in all its fascinating complexity.

Requirements: The minor in Korean requires five four-credit courses. Students have the choice of the following two options: Option 1: Take five consecutive language courses from the list of Korean language courses. Option 2: Take a minimum of four consecutive Korean language courses from the list of Korean language courses, plus a minimum of one course in Korean/East Asian culture and history offered by the Department of Modern Languages and Cultures or the Program of East Asian Studies. [13]
Description: The Korean language program at the University of Rochester guides students in learning Korean through a focus on language and cultural awareness and a communicative approach. [7, 9] The minor in Korean requires five four-credit courses. [7] Students have the choice of two options: taking five consecutive language courses or taking a minimum of four consecutive Korean language courses plus a minimum of one course in Korean/East Asian culture and history offered by the Department of Modern Languages and Cultures or the Program of East Asian Studies. [7] Learning Korean can provide students with a competitive advantage when applying to graduate schools or companies. [9] In addition to language skills, students have the opportunity to explore Korea's extensive history and culture. [9]

Requirements: To declare the minor, enrolled students are strongly encouraged to consult with the program director before submitting the online major/minor declaration form to ensure their planned courses satisfy the requirements. [9, 10] The minor itself requires the completion of a total of five courses related to Latin American and Caribbean people and their diasporas, along with a language prerequisite of Spanish or Portuguese. [7]
Description: The minor in Latin American Studies gives students a broad view of Latin American cultures and their relations to the United States and the rest of the world. [7]

Requirements:
A minor in linguistics follows the same curriculum as the major. The requirements are:

*   LING 110 Intro to Linguistic Analysis
*   LING 210(W) Intro to Language Sound Systems
*   LING 220 Intro to Syntax
*   LING 225 Intro to Semantic Analysis
*   One linguistics elective
Description: The Department of Linguistics offers a minor as well as several clusters in linguistics. A minor in linguistics follows the same curriculum as the major. Students are exposed to the same materials, methodologies, and learning experiences. This minor is an excellent background for those going on to fields such as law, education, and political science. An analytic understanding of human languages and exposure to the methods of linguistic analysis will strengthen and add depth to the student's ability to handle complex data. [7]

The department offers two undergraduate degrees: a BA in mathematics and a BS in mathematics. The BA degree is the more traditional liberal arts degree. It is the appropriate degree for students interested in a general background in mathematics, for those preparing to teach mathematics in a secondary school, and for those who want to combine a mathematics major with a study of a related field, such as a branch of engineering, physics, chemistry, biology, or economics. The BS degree is a more intensive program, designed for students with a deeper interest in mathematics. It is particularly appropriate for students who intend to go to graduate school in mathematics. Both programs can be supplemented with a variety of electives on the advice of a faculty adviser. With a few exceptions, courses are open to any undergraduate who has passed the prerequisites.

Requirements: Application requirements are for general first-year admission and not specific to the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics program. Applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a School Report, a recommendation from a school counselor, and one letter of recommendation from a teacher. Mid-year and final grade reports are also required.

Students who wish to declare a minor in mathematics must first complete a foundational course requirement before being accepted. These courses are: MATH 161: Calculus IA, MATH 162: Calculus IIA, MATH 165: Linear Algebra with Differential Equations, and one of either MATH 150: Discrete Mathematics or MATH 164: Multidimensional Calculus. [5] After completing the foundational courses, students must complete an advanced course requirement consisting of MATH 235: Linear Algebra and two additional 4-credit advanced mathematics courses (any mathematics course numbered 200 or above, except MATH 235). [5] Equivalent courses may be substituted for these requirements, and AP course credits can be used to satisfy foundational requirements. [5, 7] The process involves consulting with a departmental minor advisor and then submitting the online Major/Minor Declaration Form. [3, 6] A student must have an officially declared major before they can declare a minor. [6] A minimum GPA of 2.0 must be earned for the courses submitted for the minor. [3]
Description: The Minor in Mathematics is intended for students to explore mathematics in some depth without all the requirements of a major. [2] It consists of calculus, linear algebra, and two electives. [8] The foundational courses that must be completed before acceptance into the minor are: MATH 161: Calculus IA, MATH 162: Calculus IIA, MATH 165: Linear Algebra with Differential Equations, and one of the following: MATH 150: Discrete Mathematics or MATH 164: Multidimensional Calculus. [9] Students must then complete three advanced courses: MATH 235: Linear Algebra and two additional 4-credit advanced mathematics courses, which can be any mathematics course numbered 200 or above (except MATH 235). [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: The University of Rochester uses a holistic review process and considers applicants' academic and extracurricular achievements. While not explicitly stated as a requirement for all applicants, a writing supplement is part of the application. The university also offers a test-optional policy.
Department: Hajim School of Engineering & Applied Sciences
Description: The Department of Mechanical Engineering offers an undergraduate program leading to an accredited BS degree in mechanical engineering (ME). [4] Our students acquire knowledge in the fields of energy, material properties, fluid mechanics, solid mechanics, dynamics, laboratory techniques, design methodology, and system analysis. Our graduates apply their skills in jobs requiring engineering design, development, manufacturing, research, and resource management. The curriculum provides a balance of courses in the humanities and social sciences, physics, applied mathematics, and basic engineering. Emphasis is placed on the underlying fundamentals in the engineering course work, enabling graduates to adapt throughout their careers to rapid advances in sciences and technology. [5]
Accredidation: The BS degree program in mechanical engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET. [2]

Requirements: To declare a Minor in Mechanical Engineering, a student must already be accepted into a major. The minor requires completing four Mechanical Engineering (ME) courses at the 200 level or higher with a combined GPA of at least 2.0. [4] Students must discuss their course selections with Professor John Lambropoulos and then submit the online minor declaration form. [4, 12] No more than two courses from the minor can be used towards a separate major or minor. [4]
Description: A minor in mechanical engineering gives you a strong foundation in essential topics like thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, manufacturing, and advanced design—even if your major is in another discipline. You'll build versatile skills that apply across many industries, opening doors to careers in energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, robotics, aerospace, automotive, biomedical fields, and more. [4]

ProgramName: Minor in Medieval and Early Modern Studies

Requirements: To be admitted to the music minor, a student must submit the online Music Minor Application Form by the end of their Junior year. Admission must be declared no later than the second semester of the Junior year. After the start of the seventh semester, admission is by petition only, and students should attach a statement outlining their credentials and reasons for wishing to pursue the minor. [2] Students must also select and get an agreement from a faculty member to serve as their minor advisor. [2]
Fees: $69,030 per year for the 2025-2026 academic year. [12, 14]
Description: The minor in music requires students to engage with musical theories, materials, and techniques, the study of music in history and culture, and performance. At the same time, it provides students with the flexibility to emphasize areas that interest them most. Those enrolled in the music minor are considered members of the Department of Music and are encouraged to participate in all program activities. [1]
ScholarshipAmount: Merit-based scholarships range from $2,000 per year to full tuition coverage. [18]

Department: The Bachelor of Arts in Music is offered by the Arthur Satz Department of Music, which is part of the School of Arts & Sciences. [1, 2]
Description: The Arthur Satz Department of Music at the University of Rochester offers a bachelor of arts (BA) in music. This degree program mixes academic courses, private instruction, and ensemble experience to foster an understanding of musical languages, historical developments, and compositional styles while encouraging excellence in performance. [9] Students from all disciplines can participate in musical study and performances to acquire a deeper understanding of the many ways music and related arts reflect the values of various cultures, influence lives, and enrich human existence. [14] The program is flexible enough to allow students to pursue a double major, pre-law, or pre-medicine. [9] Students also have the option of taking courses at the renowned Eastman School of Music. [14]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [2]
AverageScholarshipAmount: Approximately half of the admitted students in the previous year were awarded a merit scholarship, with an average award of around $14,000. [28]
ScholarshipType: The University of Rochester offers merit-based scholarships for students in Arts, Sciences & Engineering. [28] One such scholarship is the Prince Street Scholarship, which recognizes high academic achievers with outstanding creative capacity. [28]

Requirements: Apply online using either the Common Application or Coalition for College Application. [2] The University of Rochester uses a holistic review process that assesses academic achievement, extracurricular engagement, and character. [2]
Description: Students in our neuroscience program will receive a BS in biological sciences: neuroscience. This program provides students an interested opportunity in biology to explore the molecular, cellular, and physiological bases of behavior. As one of the BS tracks in the University's Undergraduate Program in Biology and Medicine (UPBM), it draws upon the collective strengths of several departments on the River Campus and at the Medical Center. The major is administered by the Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences (BCS), and the core and upper-level courses in neuroscience are taught by BCS faculty. Rochester's program is one of the oldest and most distinguished undergraduate programs in neuroscience available in the United States.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Optical Engineering
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Optical Engineering, students must first apply to the Hajim School of Engineering and Applied Sciences. Applications are submitted online for either early or regular decision through the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Students officially declare their major during their sophomore year. [9]
Description: The optical engineering degree is ABET accredited and offers the same comprehensive foundation in optics offered to optics majors. The capstone experience for optical engineering majors is a senior design experience that emphasizes a team-based design process working on customer sponsored projects.
Accredidation: The optical engineering degree is ABET accredited. [13]

Requirements: The following required materials must be submitted: a completed Common Application or Coalition for College Application including the URochester-specific supplemental essay, a $50 application fee or fee waiver, a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a mid-year report from your school, and a final transcript upon enrollment. [4] International students must also submit proof of English language proficiency and a financial support form. [2, 4]
Description: The Institute of Optics is the oldest optics program in the country, awarding more than half of all optics degrees in the US. The Institute offers two majors—a BS in optics and a BS in optical engineering, and also a minor in optics. Optics majors gain a comprehensive foundation in optics along with a wide choice of elective courses that students can choose in preparation for careers in optics, photonics, imaging and laser science. [2] Both the optics and optical engineering majors have common course requirements through senior year, providing an excellent foundation in optics and opportunities to take important, skill-oriented technical electives. [2] Both options prepare students for graduate work or for a career in the field. [2] Optics is an interdisciplinary field, and professionals work in various areas including the design of optical devices, biomedical instrumentation, laser science, internet technologies, and quantum information science. [2]

Requirements: Students minoring in optics must earn a C or better in five optics courses, one of which must be laboratory-based. Complete both required optics courses: OPT 241: Geometrical Optics and OPT 261: Interference and Diffraction. Plus one of the following optics labs: OPT 201: Geometrical Optics Lab; OPT 202: Physical Optics Lab; OPT 203: Instrumentation Lab; OPT 204: Sources and Detectors Lab; or Independent research for credit. Plus two 200-level, four-credit optics courses (with the exception of OPT 287). Students interested in declaring a minor in optics should meet with a faculty member of the Institute of Optics to plan a focused program of study. [2]
Description: Optical sciences and technologies have great importance in a range of fields and applications. A stronger grasp of the field is a desirable option, particularly for majors in other science and engineering disciplines. Our optics minors get a broad introduction to optics while also being able to customize their own minor, choosing any two 200 level courses from the Institute's offerings. [3] Students minoring in optics must earn a C or better in five optics courses, one of which must be laboratory-based. [3]

Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Rochester's School of Arts, Sciences & Engineering, prospective students must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Required supporting materials include a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a school report/counselor recommendation, and a mid-year report when it becomes available. A final transcript is required upon enrollment. [8]
Concentration: Students have the option of using their philosophy electives to major with an emphasis in law and ethics, history of philosophy, or logic and the philosophy of science. These tracks will not impact how your major is listed on your transcript. [16]
Description: The undergraduate program stresses Western philosophy, both ancient and modern, and gives particular emphasis to recent and contemporary Anglo-American philosophy. The department's course offerings provide excellent foundations for graduate work in law and cognitive science, as well as in philosophy itself. [11] At Rochester, students can combine philosophy with another major. The writing and analytical skills our students learn supplement their interests in law, history, science, and more, while preparing them for graduate studies and careers. [14]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education, the New York State Board of Regents, and the Association for the Accreditation of Human Research Protection Programs. [17]

Requirements: Students who wish to declare a philosophy minor should complete the Minor Declaration Form. [2] The minor program is planned in conjunction with a departmental advisor. [2] Course requirements are 16 total credits, including at least one course at the 200-level or above and at least two courses taught by a member of the Philosophy Department. [2]
Description: The Department of Philosophy offers a general philosophy minor. [7, 8] This minor requires five courses in philosophy, with at least two being advanced courses (above PHIL 202). [7] No more than two of the five courses may be logic/science courses. [7] The department also offers specialized minors in Ethics, History of Philosophy, and Philosophy of Science. [8] The department has strengths in areas like logic, philosophy of mathematics, metaphysics, and philosophy of artificial intelligence. [14] Students can engage with topics through various course clusters, such as 'Knowledge, Mind, and Nature,' which introduces the basic methods of philosophical reasoning. [7]
Accredidation: The University of Rochester is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (MSCHE). [2, 3] This is an institutional accreditation, as MSCHE evaluates the university as a whole rather than specific academic programs. [5] The university's accreditation was most recently reaffirmed in 2024. [4] There is no specialized programmatic accreditation mentioned for the philosophy minor itself. [6]

Requirements: Application requirements are not specified for the Bachelor of Arts in Physics program. For general first-year admission, the University of Rochester requires the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a school report/counselor recommendation, and two teacher recommendations.

Admission to graduate programs in the School of Arts and Sciences and Hajim School of Engineering and Applied Sciences is highly competitive. A qualified applicant needs a strong academic record, as evidenced by high grades in relevant coursework and a strong CV/resume, as well as comprehensive letters of recommendation. [7]
Description: The BS in physics is designed for students who are interested in a career in physics or a closely related field. It provides a more in-depth treatment of the subject than the BA degree and is the appropriate choice for students who plan to continue on to graduate school in physics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Physics and Astronomy
Requirements: First-year applicants must apply online using either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. After submission, applicants can use the MyROC portal to monitor their application status and upload materials. The application process requires the submission of a personal essay through the chosen application platform.
Description: The BA program is perfect for students looking for a broad overview and the flexibility to double major. Students preparing for graduate school in physics or a related field should consider the more intensive BS program. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physics and Astronomy
Requirements: The University of Rochester requires first-year applicants to submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a school report/counselor recommendation, and one teacher recommendation. A mid-year report is also required by February 15. The university does not require an admissions interview.
Description: The BS degree is an intensive program that helps prepare students for graduate studies in astronomy, physics, or a related field. Students planning to attend graduate school normally elect the BS program. [3] Our department combines the best features of a small liberal arts college and a major research university. We are a moderately sized department with accessible faculty dedicated to excellence in teaching. [15] The BS degree is an intensive program of study providing stronger preparation for graduate school in astronomy, physics, or a closely related science, than does the BA. [15]

Requirements: To minor in physics, a student must attain an average of at least 2.0 in the introductory physics sequences and in all introductory mathematics courses. The requirements include one of the following introductory sequences: PHYS 121, 122 and 123, or PHYS 141, 142 and 143. Additionally, three 200-level physics courses are required, two of which must be from the following: PHYS 217, PHYS 218, PHYS 220, PHYS 227, PHYS 235W, PHYS 237, PHYS 243W, PHYS 244W, PHYS 245W, PHYS 246, PHYS 251, PHYS 254, or PHYS 256. [10]
Description: A physics minor is for students interested in physics but not intending to major in it. It’s also for students who may have discovered physics late in their academic career. The minor provides a basic understanding of the most essential concepts in physics and complements a variety of majors, particularly those in other sciences, engineering, and mathematics.

Requirements: To declare a minor, students should first consult the department's website to understand the course requirements. They then need to discuss their plans with the authorized faculty member in the department. After the advisor approves the plan, students can submit the online Major/Minor Declaration Form. [12] A student cannot declare a minor until they have been accepted into a major. [13]
Description: The University of Rochester's Department of Modern Languages and Cultures offers a program in Polish. [2] This program allows students to develop Polish language skills and explore the country's history and culture. [2] Learning Polish may offer a competitive advantage for students applying to graduate programs or jobs. [2] The program includes language courses at four different levels as well as courses on Polish culture and politics, which are offered by visiting faculty through the Skalny Center for Polish and Central European Studies. [2] Students also have the opportunity to study abroad at the Jagiellonian University in Kraków. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Political Science
Requirements: Required materials for first-year applicants include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a $50 application fee (with waiver available), a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation (up to three are accepted), a mid-year report, and a URochester-specific supplemental essay. [9]
Description: Political science is the study of politics and power from domestic, international, and comparative perspectives. It entails understanding political ideas, ideologies, institutions, policies, processes, and behavior, as well as groups, classes, government, diplomacy, law, strategy, and war. A background in political science is valuable for citizenship and political action, as well as for future careers in government, law, business, media, or public service.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Politics, Philosophy, and Economics
Requirements: Required application materials for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition/Scoir Application, a high school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and a school report with a counselor recommendation. Applicants must also complete the University of Rochester-specific questions, which include a supplemental essay. [2]

To apply for first-year admission, applicants must submit the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Required supporting materials include a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a school report/counselor recommendation, and a mid-year report (when available). A final transcript is required after high school completion. [6]
Description: The undergraduate psychology program offers instruction throughout the broad spectrum of behavioral science and mental life. Its content covers theoretical, empirical and technical presentations of psychology as both a social and natural science. Classes range from large lecture courses with smaller discussion sections to individual laboratories, practicums, and internships. Undergraduates may register for graduate-level courses with permission of the instructor. The program can be tailored to provide an excellent background for postgraduate work in psychology, medicine, education, social work, law, business, and other related social and natural sciences as well as to occupations in business and human services.

Requirements: Required materials for first-year applicants include the Common Application or Coalition Application, a URochester-specific supplemental essay, a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, and a school report/counselor recommendation. An application fee of $50 is also required. [1]
Description: The brain and cognitive sciences (BCS) major offers undergraduates the opportunity to study the nature and products of mental activity, including: Perception; Action; Thinking; Language; Learning; Memory. This rigorous but accessible natural science discipline lies at the intersection of cognitive psychology, computer science, and neuroscience, bringing these fields together to understand the activities of the mind and brain. Both the bachelor of arts (BA) and bachelor of science (BS) degrees are built around a common curriculum that integrates biological, behavioral, and computational approaches to the study of perception, language, thinking, learning, and the development of these capacities. [1, 2, 3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public Health
Requirements: First-year applicants must submit the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official high school transcript, a school report/counselor recommendation, and one teacher recommendation. An application fee or fee waiver is also required.
Description: At Rochester, the study of public health incorporates both the science and art of protecting and improving the health of families and communities through education and research. The public health program is designed to help students develop the many different skills that are needed to understand and respond to health challenges that arise in local, regional, and global populations. The majors share a set of common core courses across the key areas of the field, allowing students to understand health and health care from a multidisciplinary perspective.
Accredidation: Educational programs in the Department of Public Health Sciences that are accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health.

Requirements: To apply for undergraduate study at the University of Rochester, prospective students must submit either the Common Application or the Coalition for College Application. Required supporting materials include a secondary school transcript, one teacher recommendation, a school report/counselor recommendation, and a mid-year report. [7]
ScholarshipType: scholarships, grants, loans, work-study, and outside awards

Requirements: The Minor in Religion requires six courses: RELC 101: Introduction to the Hebrew Bible or RELC 102: Introduction to the New Testament; One course in the history of a religious tradition (e.g., RELC 103, 104, 105, 106, or 107); RELC 293: Theories of Religion; and three other courses in religion, selected in consultation with the student's advisor in the department. [3]
Description: The stuff we call “religion” permeates our world in powerful, subtle, violent, and creative ways. Now, as in the past, religions bind communities across time and space, illuminate souls, foster relationship between beings seen and unseen, and shape human understandings of good and evil. Drawing on the discipline's rich toolbox of diverse theoretical and methodological approaches, the religion major trains students to critically analyze religious. [17]

Requirements: Application for undergraduate admission is through the Common Application or Coalition/Scoir Application. Required materials include the application, a school report and counselor recommendation, a secondary school transcript, and one teacher recommendation. [2] International applicants must also submit proof of English proficiency. [3]
Department: School of Arts & Sciences, Department of Modern Languages and Cultures

Requirements: Five courses in Russian language, literature, and culture, to be selected in consultation with the Russian advisor. [2]
Description: The Russian curriculum at Rochester offers students courses in beginning through advanced Russian language study, Russian current events and politics, Russian literature of the last two centuries, Russian civilization, art, architecture, and film, as well as classes focusing on Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Chekhov, and Nabokov. [2] In addition, for nearly 30 years from 1992-2019, The Department of Modern Langauges and Cultures (MLC) ran its own summer program in St. Petersburg that brought scores of Rochester students to study Russian and live with Russian... The University of Rochester offers degrees in both Russian and Russian studies. [2] The Russian major, minor, and clusters are in the humanities division. [2] The Russian studies major, minor, and clusters can count in either the humanities or the social sciences. [2]

Requirements: The requirement to complete the Minor in Russian Studies is the successful completion of five courses. For a 'Russian Minor', this includes five courses in Russian language, literature, and culture, selected in consultation with the Russian advisor. [6] For a 'Russian Studies Minor', the requirement is five courses including one Russian language course at the 151-level or higher, one survey course in Russian literature, one survey course in Russian history, one course in a more specialized area of Russian history or literature, and one political science course with a Russian or international relations focus. [8]
Description: Russian studies, an interdisciplinary program of the School of Arts & Sciences, incorporates the perspective of several departments and the linguistic, historical, and cultural background needed to understand Russia's past, analyze its present, and make responsible predictions about its future. Its dynamic curriculum from three core departments includes courses on Russian history from Kievan Rus to the war in Ukraine; international relations and political science; and Russian literature, cinema and culture. Proficiency in Russian is required (coursework through intermediate Russian). [8]
ScholarshipAmount: from $2,000 per year up to full tuition fees

Requirements: Application is via the Common Application or Coalition for College Application. [6, 10] Required materials include a secondary school transcript, a school report/counselor recommendation, one teacher recommendation, and a University of Rochester supplemental essay. [10]
Description: Spanish makes an excellent and practical double major and is in high demand in fields such as medicine, social work, business, law, government, computer science, engineering, and NGOs (not-for-profits). After graduation, our Spanish majors have gone on to graduate programs in law, medicine, business, Spanish education, translation studies, public health, film, and history. Some of our graduates are employed in international business, governmental and non-governmental organizations, and community health. [2]

Requirements: A total of five courses in Spanish language, literature, and culture, to be selected in consultation with the Spanish advisor. Students usually start with SPAN 151 and may include SPAN 152, SP 200, and other 200-level courses. All minors, regardless of study-abroad credits, must take a minimum of one four-credit Spanish elective course numbered SPAN 202 or above at the University of Rochester. The Spanish minor only allows for a maximum of two courses of transfer credit, e.g. AP, IB or Education Abroad. [2]

Required application materials for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition Application, an official school transcript (including grades from 9th through 11th grade), one teacher recommendation, a mid-year report, and a supplemental essay. International students must also submit the International Financial Support Form or the CSS Profile. [4]
Description: A Bachelor of Science (BS) in Statistics offers a more specialized education_ in statistical techniques. [3] It is designed for students interested in a thorough exploration of methodology, computing, and applications, supported by a rigorous schedule of statistics and mathematics courses. The curriculum emphasizes mathematics to support advanced, upper-level statistical methodology. [3] Students in the BS program gain a strong foundation in the theoretical aspects of probability, inference, linear models, and Bayesian methods. They also develop detailed programming and computing skills relevant to the field of statistics. [3]

Requirements: The minor in statistics requires five courses: STAT 180 (formerly STAT 212), STAT 190 (formerly STAT 213), or equivalent; STAT 275, STAT 276, or STAT 277 (CSC 171 or CSC 172 may be permitted with advisor permission); and three additional 200-level STAT courses. [3] Students must achieve an overall grade of C or better in the courses used for the minor. At least four courses must be STAT-listed. [3] To declare a minor, students must first have a declared major, consult with the department's faculty advisor, and then submit an online declaration form. [9, 14]
Description: The minor in statistics is designed for students in the social and natural sciences and the humanities who are interested in statistical methodology and its application to a particular field of study. [2] The minor consists of five courses. [2] Students are required to take an introductory statistics course, a course in statistical computing, a course in probability theory, a course in mathematical statistics, and one applied statistics course from an approved list of courses. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Studio Arts
Requirements: General application requirements for first-year students include the Common Application or Coalition/Scoir Application, a URochester-specific supplemental essay, a $50 application fee (with waivers available), a secondary school transcript, a teacher recommendation (one required, up to three accepted), and a mid-year report. [2] For the Bachelor of Arts in Studio Arts specifically, a portfolio submission is not required for enrollment, but prospective students are encouraged to submit documentation of their art practice as supplementary material to their application. [17]
Description: The Department of Art and Art History offers a major in studio arts. A major in studio arts is typically declared before the junior year and requires a total of twelve courses. These include four 100-level studio courses, three 200/300-level studios in any discipline, SART 209: Writing on Art, SART 396 and 397 (senior seminar/studio), and two related courses often from art history or film and media studies. Portfolio submission is not a requirement for enrollment. The program has an honors option, which requires maintaining a 3.5 GPA in the major and completing SART 393: Senior Project, which involves both studio work and a distinguished research paper. Majors are required to present an exhibition of their work in their senior year. [15]

Requirements: A minor in studio arts requires six courses: Two or three 100-level studio courses, Two or three 200 or 300-level studio courses, One art history course. [2]

The process to add a Minor in Theatre is a declaration, not a formal application. To declare the minor, an undergraduate student must first be accepted into a major. [8, 10] The student should then consult the department's website and meet with the departmental minor advisor to create a plan for the required coursework. [8, 10] Once the plan is approved, the student submits the online Major/Minor Declaration Form. [12] The minor itself requires the completion of a minimum of 24 credits in specific theatre-related courses. [9]
Department: School of Arts & Sciences, International Theatre Program
Description: The International Theatre Program partners with the Department of English to offer a Minor in Theater. This Minor introduces students to different theatrical disciplines like production, performance, and dramatic literature. The Minor in Theater requires a minimum of 24 credits. Students who decide to study theater abroad in England can usually apply those courses towards the minor. [7]

ProgramName: Minor in Visual and Cultural Studies
